title: Submarine Cable Repair Capacities - Works
description: Expected Impact: The expected benefits of the supported project: Provide quick response to emergency situations identified by the relevant Regional Cable Hub or other entity declaring the emergency situation (Key Performance Indicator). Provide quick average estimated time-to-repair for cable systems in the targeted EU sea basins with at least one landing point in an EU territory (Key Performance Indicator). Increase operational repair capacity in the main European sea basins (Key Performance Indicator). Strengthen the resilience of cable systems in the main European sea basins. Ensure digital sovereignty and strategic autonomy of the EU in the main European sea basins. Objective: This call aims to enhance emergency response capacities and the resilience of backbone networks’ infrastructures by supporting the development and deployment of adaptable repair modules for swift emergency repair operations, enabling quick response to incidents that could severely impact the Union or its Member States. The goal of the EU is to fund modules covering the main sea basins of the Union, the objective being to develop adaptable repair modules that can be deployed on existing vessels, as well as the necessary related operational capabilities. The modules are expected to be rapidly operational in order to re-establish the service of submarine cables (through repair or substitution) in emergency situations, i.e. where the cut or the failure of the cable can cause a severe damage to one or more Member States, and the service disruption cannot be fixed timely by commercial services. Applicants will have to work in coordination with the authorities declaring the emergency situation, which are expected to be the future Regional Cable Hubs4. The modules would be hosted in ports or shipyards with the capacity to install them on board of ships within a maximum of 3 days from the arrival of the vessel at the port/shipyard, following a request by the Regional Surveillance Hub envisaged in the Action Plan on Cable Security . Scope: This call funds modular equipment for the repair of telecom submarine cables, and targets public entities with an emergency response mandate such as entities active in the civil protection, national emergency response agencies, coastguards and military navies. Each Member State will confirm the nature of the applicant in the mandatory Letter of Support. Beneficiaries can subcontract the activities covered by this call for proposals as well as the operation of the modules for repair intervention to third parties, including publicly or privately owned entities without an emergency response mandate. However, the modules can only be used to respond to emergency situations declared by the competent authority. The pre-configured vessels are flat deck vessels that should be able to receive the modules with minor adaptation and operational preparation, and without regulatory or technical barriers. Therefore, the proposals should demonstrate the adaptability, portability and scalability of the solution put forward. To make sure that the modular equipment will be ready for intervention, applicants should identify at least three vessels that are or will be pre-configured for receiving the modules. Costs for pre-configuration of the vessels can be included in the proposal provided that they comply with the eligibility conditions of this call. Applicants should explain in detail in their proposal how the vessels are already pre-configured or how they plan to carry out the above-mentioned pre-configuration, and how many pre-configured vessels will be made available. For vessels owned by third parties, applicants should provide details on lease or service level agreement guaranteeing the availability of these vessels to receive the modules over their economic lifespan (at least 10 years). Proposals should also demonstrate solid implementation plans, including the definition of compatible specifications for the vessels and the different types of modules, project’s phasing (design, production-level deployment, operation), governance, allocation policies, financial aspects, as well as the rationale for the choice of the storage and installation locations. To this purpose, it is crucial that the proposals clearly demonstrate effective, reliable and efficient coordination with all relevant stakeholders, especially the entity declaring the emergency situation which is expected to be the future Regional Cable Hubs. The solidity of the plan will be taken into account when assessing the maturity of the proposal. Proposals should demonstrate how they contribute to CPEI Area 8 (“Multipurpose vessel(s) and modular equipment stock”) from the CPEI list published in February 2026 , and in particular to one or more of the CPEI criteria b, c, d and e of Point 26, and CPEI criteria a, b and c of Point 27 of Commission Recommendation (EU) 2024/779 . Proposals must provide repair modules to increase repair capacity for all subsea cable systems, serving EU Member States in the main European sea basins following the current repair agreements when relevant. Please consult the call document for more information on the scope, including digital security requirements.

eligibilityText: Rooted in the EU founding principles of human dignity, freedom and democracy, RIZA’s main mission is to build capacity of and provide financial support to small-scale grassroots NGOs across the EU to uphold, protect and promote EU values and fundamental rights, focussing on those in most isolated circumstances with least access to resources and opportunities, i.e. migrant and refugee women. With 3 rounds of funding in total (2025, 2026 and 2027), this 2nd RIZA call has a regional focus on the Southern-Mediterranean states (Spain, Portugal, Italy, Greece, Cyprus, Malta) in which the organisations in the region are particularly encouraged to apply, however, RIZA funding is open to any qualified organisations established in any EU members state. The call is open to the following organisations, Tier 1 constituting the priority group among the potential grantees: Tier 1 : Migrant and/or refugee women led organisations with a human right based mission. Tier 2 : Grassroots women’s rights organisations with a stand-alone programme aimed at supporting migrant and/or refugee women. Tier 3 : Migrant and/or refugee organisations with a stand-alone programme aimed at supporting migrant and/or refugee women. Tier 4: Grassroots human rights organisations with a stand-alone programme aimed at supporting migrant and/or refugee women. Call’s Priorities : • Priority 1 : Support and Capacity Building of Migrant and Refugee women • Priority 2 : Advocating for the fundamental rights of migrant and refugee women • Priority 3 : Promoting the role of migrant and refugee women in democratic dialogue, community cohesion and cross-cultural solidarity For eligible activities under each Priority, please consult detailed information in the call for proposals. Available grants • 16 Micro Grants of Euro 17778 • 12 Small Grants of Euro 32778 • 6 Medium Grants of Euro 60000 Application process: 1 stage : eligibility, admissibility and general relevance. 2 stage : shortlisted candidates only, evaluation of relevance, quality and impact. An information session is foreseen on: Tuesday 9th June 2026 10:00-12:00 CET For more information please visit: www.migrantwomennetwork.org/riza Contact: riza@migrantwomennetwork.org

eligibilityText: The CoPower Action has been designed to directly fund initiatives addressing Gender Based Violence(GBV) against women, girls and children through an intersectional approach . All eligible activities supported through the project calls will directly respond to the multidimensional and intersecting needs of women, girls, and child survivors of GBV, strengthening an inclusive and accessible protection systems across different intervention contexts. Child protection and gender mainstreaming are expected to be integral components of the proposals submitted by CSOs, while partner organisations will provide dedicated technical support to improve the capacities of participating CSOs in these areas. 3 NATIONAL CALLS Three national calls will support CSOs in Italy, Greece and Spain focusing on: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV . TARGET APPLICANTS The calls target small and medium-sized grassroots CSOs , particularly those operating in rural, peripherical or marginalised areas and legally registered in Italy, Greece or Spain. The primary target group, will include Women’s rights organisations (WROs), Anti-violence centres and anti-trafficking centres, Human rights, LGBTIQ+ rights, child rights, social inclusion and disability, elderly, migrant and refugee organisations. 2 FUNDING WORKSTREAMS: 1. Enhanced protection response for women, girls and children, victims of GBV, adopting an intersectional approach. This area focusses on providing tailored protection and support services, including safe houses, medical and psychological assistance for women and girls, in all their diversity, who are victims of domestic, sexual violence and other forms of GBV considering specific barriers for equal access to protection (Budget: 540,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). 2. Reduction of harmful practices , with a focus on improving interventions against harmful practices such as female genital mutilation, intersex genital mutilation, forced abortion, forced sterilisation, child and forced marriage, and honour-related violence, forced medicalisation of transgender women. Funded projects will aim at both 9 preventing and responding to these practices, with a particular focus on raising awareness, strengthening legal frameworks, and providing education to communities at risk (Budget: 360,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). CALL TIMELINE First Round : Opening: 24/08/2026 ( 11/09/2026 in Greece) Deadline: 23/11/2026 at 15.00 CET Second Round : Opening: 01/12/2026 Deadline: 01/03/2027 at 15.00 CET AVAILABLE GRANT PER COUNTRY : First Round - 6 projects of the following amounts will be awarded: Stream 1: one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 20,000 Stream 2: one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 25,000; one grant of EUR 5,000 Second Round - 4 projects of the following amounts will be awarded: Stream 1: one grant of EUR 30,000; one grant of EUR 30,000; Stream 2: one grant of EUR 20,000; one grant of EUR 20,000 APPLICATION PROCESS: Administrative check Eligibility requirements verification and shortlisting Final assessment and selection Pre-notification and Due diligence Confirmation and signing the agreement Information session are foreseen online and in present in each country. For more information please visit: https://copower.oxfam.it/ Contact: infocopower@oxfam.it
furtherInformation:
The CoPower project is implemented by Oxfam Italia ETS, Action Aid Hellas, Asociación Bienestar y Desarolloa and We World-GVC. It started on 1 March 2026 and will end on 28 February 2029.

Its objective is to strengthen the capacity of Civil Society Organisation (CSOs) to provide safe and inclusive services for victims of gender-based violence (GBV) against women, girls, and children in all their diversity across six European countries: Italy, Greece, Spain, Serbia, Romania, and Albania.

The project foresees three national calls, along with transnational calls involving the following country pairs: Italy–Serbia, Spain-Romania, and Greece-Albania. The national calls will fund at least 10 projects in Italy, 10 in Spain and 10 in Greece. The transnational calls will fund 5 projects for Italy and Serbia, 5 projects for Spain and Romania and 5 projects for Greece and Albania. Overall, a minimum of 60 CSOs will be engaged, fostering meaningful cross-country cooperation.

A comprehensive capacity-sharing programme for CSOs will include needs assessments, training, mentoring, and both national and international workshops to promote mutual learning and support in the full implementation of the EU Violence Against Women Directive.

title: Strengthening the remembrance of Roma victims
description: Objective: 3. Strengthening the remembrance of the Holocaust, acts of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity to strengthen democracy in the EU. Projects under this topic should focus on the non-Jewish victims of the Holocaust as well as other genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity of the 20 th century’s Europe. Projects under this topic should NOT address the Holocaust against Jewish people which are covered by Topic 2. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-GENCRIME-1 - Priority 1: Strengthening the remembrance of Roma victims The genocide of Roma and Sinti under Nazi rule, known as Porajmos or Samudaripen, is a defining yet insufficiently recognized legacy for the European Union. An estimated 500,000 Roma, including Sinti and Travellers, were murdered, and countless others were persecuted, deported, forcibly sterilized, and subjected to inhuman treatment. The Nazi regime implemented racial policies aimed at the systematic destruction of Roma communities across Europe, culminating in mass killings such as the liquidation of the Roma camp at Auschwitz-Birkenau on 2 August 1944, now commemorated as European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. The Roma Holocaust must be understood within a longer continuum of antigypsyism in Europe. Roma were enslaved for nearly five centuries in the territories of present-day Romania, deprived of legal personhood and basic rights. In the 20th century, persecution continued under fascist and communist regimes and, in several countries, through forced sedentarisation, assimilation policies, and coercive practices including forced sterilizations. These historical injustices have had lasting socio-economic consequences. Despite this, Roma persecution remains underrepresented in school curricula, museums, and public memorials. Dedicated research centres, permanent monuments, and teaching materials on Roma history and the Roma Holocaust are limited. This structural invisibility contributes to persistent antigypsyism, distortion, and denial. As survivor numbers decline, preserving testimonies, memorial sites, and archival materials becomes increasingly urgent. Commemorative initiatives such as 2 August – European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day – and 16 May – Romani Resistance Day require stronger institutional support and integration into European remembrance culture. Current political developments also demonstrate the vulnerability of Roma Holocaust memory. Historical distortion, trivialization, and denial — often intertwined with broader antigypsyist narratives — undermine democratic values. Memory competition and selective recognition of victimhood risk reinforcing exclusion. Citizens must be empowered to counter distortion, denial, and the minimization of the Roma genocide. In line with the EU Roma Strategic Framework for Equality Inclusion and Participation 2020-2030, special priority will be given to projects that strengthen Roma Holocaust remembrance while addressing the deeper roots of antigypsyism. Projects under this priority could focus on: Documenting the implementation of the Roma genocide and its historical context, including slavery, post-war persecution and totalitarian persecutions. Countering denial, distortion, trivialization, and the marginalization of Roma victimhood. Developing networks of Roma and non-Roma youth ambassadors to promote remembrance and counter antigypsyism. Supporting grassroots commemorative initiatives, including activities marking 2 August – European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day, 16 May – Romani Resistance Day, etc. Developing and disseminating teaching materials that integrate Roma history and the Roma Holocaust into national curricula. Digitalizing testimonies, archival documents, and historical research to preserve memory for future generations. Promoting research on Roma restitution, forced displacement, and long-term consequences of historical injustice. Collecting, documenting and disseminating stories of Roma resistance, heroes, rescuers, intellectuals, artists and community leaders, highlighting Roma agency, resilience and contribution to European history. Applying transitional justice approaches, including truth-seeking, recognition of harm, restitution research, and guarantees of non-repetition through education and memorialization. Developing inclusive, participatory ways to remember, educate about, and teach about these crimes in order to prevent the resurgence of hatred, including antigypsyism. This may include artistic memory projects, memory activism, and other approaches that foster an enabling learning environment. For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document .

title: Strengthening the remembrance of LGBTIQ+ victims and other victims
description: Objective: 3. Strengthening the remembrance of the Holocaust, acts of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity to strengthen democracy in the EU. Projects under this topic should focus on the non-Jewish victims of the Holocaust as well as other genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity of the 20 th century’s Europe. Projects under this topic should NOT address the Holocaust against Jewish people which are covered by Topic 2. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-GENCRIME-2 - Priority 2: Strengthening the remembrance of LGBTIQ+ victims and other victims Projects under this priority should not address projects focusing on the remembrance of Roma victims (Projects focussing on the remembrance of Roma victims should apply under Priority 1 ). Europe’s 20th century was marked by horrific crimes, genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity as well as the crimes committed under authoritarian and totalitarian regimes, including those of communist and fascist dictatorships. The remembrance of these gravest crimes committed on European soil plays a critical role in upholding these values. Despite growing efforts to preserve the memory of the victims of these crimes, the experiences of many groups remain overlooked, marginalised or insufficiently recognised in public memory. This includes, among others, LGBTIQ+ people and other communities targeted on the basis of their identity, beliefs or perceived social status. Throughout history, LGBTIQ+ people have faced systemic persecution under a wide range of political and social regimes, often shaped by prevailing religious, cultural, and legal norms. Under the Nazi regime, it is estimated that 50000 gay and bisexual men were subject to ‘severe jail sentences in brutal conditions’, with around 10-15000 being sent to concentration camps. Lesbian women, transgender people, and others whose identities did not conform to Nazi ideals of gender and sexuality also faced surveillance, discrimination, violence, and social exclusion, with their experiences largely unrecognized for decades. As a result, the history of LGBTIQ+ persons in Europe is marked by both struggle and resilience. The preservation and recognition of LGBTIQ+ history and memory are essential to building an inclusive European identity rooted in dignity, diversity, and human rights. Remembering and recognising these atrocities is essential to restore justice as underlined in the LGBTIQ+ equality strategy 2026-2030. Greater awareness of all these histories contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of the causes, mechanisms and consequences of mass atrocities and contributes not only to preventing their recurrence but also to reinforcing democratic resilience, fostering civic engagement, and building a common European culture of remembrance. Projects under this topic could focus on: Addressing how genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity were organised, which actors were involved and how they were committed, the roles of collaborators, perpetrators and bystanders. Finding new ways of remembering, educating and teaching about these crimes to protect society against resurging threats of hatred. They can include artistic work on memory projects, as well as stimulating memory activism. These new methods should be inclusive, where applicable participatory and create an enabling learning environment. Fostering awareness raising, mutual learning or training activities that accurately reflect the persecution of LGBTIQ+ people, and other minorities throughout history. Countering historical falsification and memory competition related to the persecution of LGBTIQ+ people, genocides, war crimes and crimes against humanity, especially among Europeans that shared a common history but have divergent views on their common past. Fostering awareness raising, mutual learning or training activities that accurately reflect the persecution of LGBTIQ+ people, and other minorities under the Nazi regime while countering denial, distortion, trivialization, and especially false comparisons. Addressing divergent and opposite national historical narratives, on regional basis, of these darkest hours of Europe history and other negative common shared historical events. Digitalising historical material and testimonies of witnesses for education and training purposes. For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document .

title: Fostering remembrance of the legacy of colonialism, slavery, and migration, and their impact on contemporary multicultural European societies.
description: Objective: 4. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-HISTMIGRATION - Fostering remembrance of the legacy of colonialism, slavery, and migration, and their impact on contemporary multicultural European societies. Migration, de-colonisation, enslavement, and imperialism have left a mark on global history and are embedded in the European history, with profound consequences for society today. Their remembrance plays a key role in combating structural racism, empowering people impacted by racism, and raising awareness of exclusion and stereotypes. While for many it is considered a chapter in history, de-colonisation, the dismantlement of colonial empires particularly in the 20th century and the emerging post-colonial European societies continue to have harsh consequences in the lives of people facing racism and racial discrimination. Following the decolonisation process in international relations in the early 20th century, the UN World Conference on Combating Racism, Racial Discrimination, and Xenophobia established that today’s structural inequalities are caused by the consequences of colonialism and slavery. Stemming from this observation, in its EU Anti-Racism Action Plan 2020-2025 and EU Anti-Racism Strategy 2026–2030, the Commission made efforts to communicate on addressing the historical roots of racism and established a key priority to combat structural racism. This entails an examination of the past, present and future of the cultural fabric of Europe. Prejudices and stereotypes can be addressed by acknowledging the historical roots of racism, including from an intersectional perspective. Migration has also a long and varied history in Europe. Population movements in Europe, from economic, political migration to expulsion and deportation after the Second World War, from fleeing violence and persecution to migration after the creation of the EU, have marked 20th century European history. Forced migration, internal displacement and expulsion is an experience shared by many Europeans during the period of war. This includes the forced displacement and persecution of Roma populations during and after the Second World War, and its long-term consequences. The specific history of female migration can also be considered. Projects in this priority should contribute to a better understanding of how these historical legacies - rooted in colonialism, enslavement an imperialism - shape contemporary inequalities, discrimination, exclusion and barriers to equal opportunities in European societies. Projects are encouraged to examine the links between these historical legacies and contemporary manifestations of structural racism, including anti-Black racism, antigypsyism, antisemitism, anti-Muslim hatred and anti-Asian racism. Projects under this topic could focus on: Acknowledging the legacy of colonialism and its ongoing impact on contemporary multicultural European societies, with a view to contributing to the objectives of the EU Anti-Racism Strategy 2026–2030, including addressing topics such as structural discrimination and racism. Promoting anti-racism education, historical literacy and awareness-raising initiatives aimed at young people, educators and wider society, including through innovative and participatory approaches that foster mutual respect, inclusion and democratic values. Supporting the collection, preservation and dissemination of testimonies, archives and community-based knowledge that contribute to a stronger evidence base on the historical roots and contemporary manifestations of racism and discrimination in Europe. Raising awareness of Roma history and culture to contribute to strengthening multicultural European societies, in line with the EU Roma Strategic Framework for equality, inclusion and participation. Examining common European experiences of migration linked to historical events such as wars, transition moments, colonisation and de-colonisation, economic impacts, or persecution. Adopting an intersectional approach to cover several minority groups, including People of African descent, Jews, Roma, overseas citizens, and other minority groups with a long history of migration, to promote a more nuanced understanding of multicultural European societies. For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document .

title: Strengthening the remembrance of the Holocaust against Jewish people.
description: Objective: 2. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-HOLOCAUSTJEW - Strengthening the remembrance of the Holocaust against Jewish people. The Shoah is a defining legacy for the EU. Six million Jewish children, women and men were murdered, and all others were persecuted. While other groups were persecuted, the Nazis have set up across Europe and beyond a state policy with the sole aim to kill every single Jews they could find. First-hand accounts of the Shoah continue to have the most powerful impact on following generations. As there are less and less survivors to share the story of their survival, the importance of memorial sites and education increases, as well as the work done by second and third generations of survivors and associations. Current events show the instrumentalization of the Holocaust by Kremlin propaganda claiming to denazify Ukraine. In parallel, there is also an increasing politicization of the Holocaust in several EU Member States, and a tendency to minimize the atrocities of the Shoah. In addition, since the 7 October 2023 attacks by Hamas and the wars that ensued, we have seen a growing conflation of the Shoah with the conflicts in the Middle East. Citizens should be empowered to counter this conflation. Holocaust distortion fuels antisemitism. In addition, hate speech relating to the condoning, denial or gross trivialisation of the Holocaust is criminalised under the Council Framework Decision on combating certain forms and expressions of racism and xenophobia by means of criminal law 4 . Wounds of mass atrocities of the 20th century are still open today, fuelling divergences among Europeans. Free, open and independent research, education and memory on all aspects of the Shoah is essential to increase understanding. This implies exploring Europe’s negative history with the aim to reconcile divergent regional and national narratives related to the Shoah and its immediate aftermath. European citizens should become ambassadors of this memory. Teachers, policymakers, university students (especially history students) could be among key target audiences and be empowered to develop a common European history, to counter historical falsification, distortion and inversion. Target groups could include local public authorities and policy makers, to raise awareness about their responsibility to safeguard the sites and combat antisemitism. Target groups could include newcomers and migrants that do not have a direct link with the Shoah. Target groups could also include journalists, to raise awareness about Holocaust distortion, Holocaust inversion and Holocaust-related contemporary events (such as for example Neo-Nazi marches). In line with the EU Strategy on combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life (2021-2030), as well as with other key policy initiatives, this topic supports projects that can focus on developing networks of Young European Ambassadors to promote Shoah remembrance. This topic will also support projects that contribute to Holocaust sites especially regarding their educational purposes, and encourage cooperation with ESHEM, the network of European Sites of Holocaust Memory. Jewish communities are today small, as a direct consequence from the Holocaust. This results in direct responsibility to support Jewish life and raise awareness about Jewish presence in Europe. Projects under this topic could focus on: Addressing how the Shoah took place, how the crimes were committed, which actors were involved, as well as pre-war and immediate postwar historical developments. Countering Holocaust denial, distortion, trivialisation and victims’ inversion. This includes countering false comparisons, antisemitic conspiracy theories, and conflation with the Middle East conflict. Monitoring and countering on the online sphere Holocaust distortion and inversion, as well as Nazi glorification. Addressing divergent and opposite national historical narratives, on regional basis, of the history of the Shoah, including parallelism with other negative common shared historical regional events. Promoting memory activism related to the Shoah including by supporting grassroot commemorative work. Digitalising historical material and testimonies of witnesses for education and training purposes. Shedding light on Jewish life before and after the Shoah. Raising awareness on Jewish life, history and culture, to contribute to strengthening multicultural European societies. Marking International Holocaust Remembrance Day and national Holocaust remembrance days. Raise awareness on the Shoah and memorial sites at local level, including through visits of local authorities. Combating glorification of Nazism, countering neo-Nazis manifestations and activities. Promoting provenance research on looted art to foster awareness raising, mutual learning or training activities. For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document . 4 Council Framework Decision 2008/913/JHA of 28 November 2008 on combating certain forms and expressions of racism and xenophobia by means of criminal law, EUR-Lex - 32008F0913 - EN - EUR-Lex

title: European Platforms for the promotion of emerging artists
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The European Festivals Fund for Emerging Artists – EFFEA, an initiative of the European Festivals Association, is a fund that supports collaborations between festivals from different countries. Together, these festivals provide emerging artists with a platform to develop their work and gain visibility on the international stage. EFFEA extends an open invitation for festivals to collaborate across borders and establish a network of colleagues centred around the concept of a residency. Through EFFEA, festivals join hands to foster the success of emerging artists. EFFEA's fifth call for festivals to support emerging artists is open from 1 September to 3 November 2026 . 50 residencies will be selected involving 50 emerging artists (individuals, groups or collectives) in the seat of around 150 festivals, a leading festival in collaboration with a minimum of two partner festivals each. There are two categories of residencies: 1. EFFEA Discovery: Festivals support artists at the early stages of their careers but with a strong potential to break through internationally. 40 grants of 8.000€ will be attributed to this category. 2. EFFEA Springboard : Festivals support artists already established in their own country and ready to develop their careers internationally. 10 grants of 15.000€ will be attributed to this category. Eligibility criteria The partnership must represent at least 3 festivals from 3 eligible countries (1 leading festival and 2 partner festivals). Both leading and partner festivals must exist for at least one edition. Both leading and partner festivals must be registered on www. FestivalFinder.eu before submitting their application. A festival may apply for one grant as a leading festival and is eligible to apply for multiple grants as a partner festival. Proposed artists may be individual artists, collectives, companies, ensembles, or groups of any age and nationality. Artists must have either nationality or legal residence in one of the eligible countries. Eligible Countries Leading festivals and artists should have their official address in one of the following eligible countries: Albania, Armenia, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Georgia, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Montenegro, Moldova, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Tunisia, Ukraine. Festivals with their official address from the following countries are allowed to participate as partner festivals only : Israel, Palestine, Switzerland, Turkey, and the UK. Artists from these countries can also be proposed. Eligible disciplines Festivals and artists work in one or more of the following artistic disciplines: Architecture, Ballet, Contemporary Dance, Circus, Design/ Applied arts, Digital arts, Film, Folklore and folk arts, Heritage, Interdisciplinary, Literature, Music, Opera, Street Art, Theatre, Photography/ Video, Puppetry, Sculpture, Painting. Conditions and Selection Criteria The start and end dates of the residency must fall within the implementation period. This means that the residency start date must be no earlier than 1 January 2027 , and the end date must be no later than 31 December 2027 . If applicants start the residency earlier or end it later, any costs related to the extended period must not be included in the budget submitted to EFFEA. Submitted proposals will be assessed for eligibility by the EFA team. All eligible proposals will be evaluated by the EFFEA Jury, composed of members with diverse profiles in terms of artistic disciplines, geographies, backgrounds, gender, age, and, above all, with knowledge of the arts field. The selection criteria assume that: The residency is relevant for the artists, festivals and audiences. It will have an impact on the artists’ careers. It offers a market to artists even beyond the residency period (longer term). The budget is built on the principle of fair remuneration towards the artists at all stages (stay, rehearsal time and payment, fees, etc.). The topics of today focus on diversity, sustainability (ecological, cultural, artistic, economic and social), digital tools and inclusion. These can be cited as motivation and will be considered in evaluating the quality of the residency. Submission The leading festival must submit the application online via the EFFEA website . Applications cannot be submitted in any other way. The leading festival will be asked to fill in: General information about leading festival/ organisation. Information about the proposed artists, including short biographies and links (text and/or audiovisual). General information about the partner festivals. Motivation for supporting the artists and establishing the partnership for the residency. Letter of intent with the artists (template available for download). Letter of intent with the partner festivals (template available for download). A detailed budget form (template available to download). The Leading Festivals must Upload and sign all required documents (including the budget and letters of intent with the artists and the partner festivals). Ensure that the proposed residency dates fall within the eligible implementation period. Ensure that the proposed artists meet the EFFEA eligibility criteria regarding previous participation. Artists who received a Discovery grant through a previous EFFEA Call remain eligible for a Springboard residency under Call #5. Applications will be evaluated in November 2026. Applicants will be notified of the results by email in December 2026.

title: Supporting Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations to co-create/showcase
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK), together with Trans Europe Halles (SE), announce the second call for proposals for the co-creation funding of international cooperation projects. The objective of the call is to support co-creation between Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations and their peers from Creative Europe countries on the topic of resilience. Funding will be available for co-creation projects involving at least one Ukrainian partner and a partner from another Creative Europe participating country. Each partner is expected to play a role of comparable weight in the project — whether through creative input, management responsibilities, or audience development. All creative sectors are eligible, with the exception of the audio-visual sector. Each co-creation project must include a public presentation in the locality of every participating partner. Purpose of the call: To develop and present an international co-creation on the topic of resilience, in any artistic/cultural sector except audio-visual. To carry out at least two local presentations (one/locality, including in Ukraine) Budget: — Total funding available 187,500€ — Amounts per grant: Up to 25,000€, covering up to 90% of project costs. — Applicants are expected and required to provide the rest of the total project budget as a contribution. — Expected number of grants 7-10 Eligible applicants: Organisations active in the field of arts and culture established in a Creative Europe country ( EU countries , non-EU countries ). For Ukraine, they must be registered in a zone effectively controlled by the Ukrainian government . Projects must include at least two partners from at least two countries, of which one is Ukraine. Individual artists and freelancers cannot apply directly; they must take part through an eligible organisation acting as a project partner. List of activities that are eligible for financial support: — All activities necessary for the co-creation project implementation and development. — Presentation of the co-creation in the locality of each project partner. — Travel related to organisational, rehearsal, artistic, presentation purposes. Duration of the project: — project duration period: up to 7 months within the indicative implementation window of February–August 2027; — earliest start of the project after the signature of the grant agreement. Technical eligibility criteria: all required attachments (as described in the Application Procedure below) are uploaded to the platform in separate files and in the formats specified for this call; all required attachments are uploaded to the platform following standard templates that can be downloaded on the platform; all required attachments are readable, accessible, and printable; all the project partners meet the eligibility conditions specified for this call; the registration of all the project partners meets the conditions specified for this call; the application form is complete and contains all the requested information; the total subgrant amount requested in the budget is within the maximum subgrant amounts determined for this call; the total project partners contribution meets the conditions specified for this call; project implementation period is within the project implementation period defined for this call; the start of project implementation meets the conditions specified for this call. Selection criteria: Relevance: — relevance of the project to the objectives of the call; — relevance of potential co-creation to act as a basis for intercultural dialogue. Quality: — quality of extent to which cross-cutting issues (digital, green, inclusion) are addressed, including barrier-free access to project results; — quality of the partnership: the equal importance of the roles played by project partners; — quality of scale of engagement, measured by the expected audience size and number of local presentations. Impact: — Impact and the sustainability of the project, including plans and possibilities for future presentations of the co-creation. Selection procedure: Applications will first undergo a technical eligibility check by the ZMINA:Resilience team to verify that they meet all formal requirements, including admissibility and eligibility criteria. Proposals that pass this stage will then be assigned to two independent evaluators each. Evaluators will assign scores to applications. Then, the applications will be rated according to the average score. The final selection will be made by the Selection Committee, taking into account geographical, sectoral, and thematic diversity, within the available budget of the call. The application budget will be assessed for cost-effectiveness and plausibility, and may be adjusted before the grant agreement is signed. The final grant amount will be determined based on a combination of lump sum units and actual costs incurred: costs such as artist fees, travel, accommodation, and per diems are paid at the fixed unit rates listed under "Eligible costs covered by the grant" below, regardless of the exact amount spent, while costs such as equipment rental, production services, and shipping are reimbursed based on actual costs incurred. Due to the volume of applications received, the ZMINA:Resilience project team will not be able to provide individual feedback for selection decisions. All decisions are final. Application Procedure — Applications must be submitted via the IZOLYATSIA online platform no later than 04.12.2026, 23:59 Kyiv time / 22:49 Central European Time on https://platform.izolyatsia.org/en/contest/zmina-resilience-cocreation-two . — Applicant: The application shall be submitted by a single representative of the consortium/project partners (Lead Applicant). Required Documents: The application form and budget (completed directly on the platform), Supporting documents regarding capacity, eligibility, and admissibility. The following must be uploaded to the platform in .pdf format separately for each partner: A scanned copy of the Letter of Guarantee , completed and signed by the head of the applicant organization (template available for download on the platform); Registration documents for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: national registration documents with English translation in case the document is issued in another language. Registration documents for organisation from Ukraine: Full Extract from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, Physical Persons-Entrepreneurs, and Public Formations dated on or after 5 October 2026 - in their original language. The current version of the Statutes or equivalent (if mandatory for the legal entity) – all pages: for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: with English translation in case the document is issued in another language, for organisation from Ukraine: in their original language. Language of application: The application must be submitted in English. Support: During the application period, assistance will be provided through Q&A sessions and a dedicated email helpline. Subgrant Agreement Template Funding Conditions — Financial support: 70% is disbursed upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining amount is paid upon submission and approval of the report. — Co-financing is mandatory and must be at least 10% of the total project budget. — Double funding within the EU budget is not allowed. — All costs must be incurred after the grant agreement is signed and within the project implementation period. — Compliance with EU branding and visibility requirements is mandatory . Eligible costs covered by the grant include Daily fee for artistic work: 75€/artist/day Travel: International: 350€/return trip or Local (e.g. participation in trainings): 65€/return trip Support to green travel (in addition to the travel rate above, for one-way trips over 600km not made by air): 300€ Accommodation & per diem: 75€/overnight Visa cost, if needed: 80€ Shipping/Transport (of equipment), incl. insurance: at cost; Supplies & equipment (for equipment depreciation costs only): at cost; Services required for project implementation (production, rental of equipment, rental of space for project events, etc.): at cost; Communication, marketing and documentation: at cost. Management and administration costs: Max. 20% of the overall project budget (grant amount plus own contribution/co-financing combined). Estimated dates: — Launch of the Call for Proposals: 5 October 2026 — Deadline for Submission of Applications: until 23:59 4December 2026 (Kyiv time) — Evaluation Period: December 2026 — Announcement of Results: January 2027 — Signing of Grant Agreements: February 2027 — Implementation of Selected Projects: February 2027 – August 2027 (each project runs up to 7 months within this window, depending on its grant agreement signing date)

title: Fostering Ukrainians’ access to culture and cultural heritage
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Culture Helps Solidarity - Open Call for Individual Grant Sixth round, 12 October - 26 October 2026 Culture Helps Solidarity supports arts and culture professionals from Ukraine to sustain creativity, resilience, and community connection during and after the war. Running until 2028, the project combines three grant schemes - individual grants, thematic project grants, and collaboration grants - with a rich programme of mentoring, learning, and peer exchange. The project is co-funded through the Creative Europe programme and implemented by the European Cultural Foundation (Amsterdam), an independent foundation fostering European belonging through culture; together with Insha Osvita (Kyiv), a Ukrainian NGO and professional learning community developing educational and cultural programmes; zusa (Berlin), an international NGO fostering collaboration and collective learning for social and cultural change; and the VETERANKA Movement (Kyiv), Ukraine's leading community of women veterans advocating for women's rights, leadership, and reintegration. The Individual Grants provide direct, flexible support to cultural professionals in and from Ukraine who are working - often voluntarily - with displaced people and refugees, veterans and vulnerable communities, in Ukraine or in any of the Creative Europe (CE) countries (which include the 27 EU Member States and more countries participating in Creative Europe ). These personal care grants are designed to offer quick and accessible assistance for strengthening the personal wellbeing, resilience and mental health of cultural professionals and creatives, enabling them to continue their crucial cultural, community-based work in extremely challenging circumstances. These grants are not designed to cover costs related to project delivery or implementation. This is the sixth call in the series of rolling application rounds, opening approximately every six weeks. Across the 2026-2028 project period, we anticipate 10–14 such cycles. In each cycle, approximately 7 to 10 grants of up to EUR 1,200 will be disbursed. WHO IS IT FOR? This call seeks to support individual professionals in need for individual wellbeing care who work in arts, culture or community-based cultural activities and: support displaced Ukrainians, both inside Ukraine and across Creative Europe countries; play a meaningful and publicly relevant role for maintaining cultural production, artistic creation or community life in Ukraine or in Creative Europe countries; work with veterans and vulnerable groups; seek urgent personal wellbeing support that will enable them to continue their work, creative practice, and engagement with their communities; have been personally affected by war, displacement, and/or traumatic working conditions. WHAT DO WE OFFER? We offer up to €1,200 (including taxes if applicable) per individual, disbursed as a one-off contribution. The grant may be used strictly for personal mental health and wellbeing support and may not be directed to third parties, to project implementation or organisational costs. Eligible activities include: Psychotherapy or psychological counselling; Trauma-informed coaching or emotional (group) support sessions; Restorative care or rehabilitation stays (e.g., sanatorium treatment, wellness programmes, retreats); Visit to cultural institutions and events (tickets to museums, theatres, cinemas, concerts, etc.); Participation in master classes or workshops (art therapy) and materials for participation in them, if necessary; Other justified wellbeing-oriented services that directly support the applicant’s resilience. The grant may not be used for: psychiatric consultations or medical mental‑health treatment (including any expenses that involve medical care, diagnosis); purchase of medication or medical devices (even if prescribed by a doctor); purchase of material assets (tools, household items, equipment, etc., consumables for work, etc.); payment of rent for premises (residential or commercial, non-residential); tuition fees, other training costs (formal or informal); invasive interventions (surgical operations, cosmetic procedures, dental interventions, etc.); streaming platform subscriptions; consultations with doctors of alternative medical practice; strictly humanitarian needs or cost-of-living support. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Individual grants are strictly dedicated to individuals, who: are aged 18 and above; reside in Ukraine or have fled from Ukraine to one of the Creative Europe countries (which include the 27 EU Member States and more countries participating in Creative Europe ); artists, cultural managers, or activists and volunteers working with displaced persons in Ukraine, or with displaced persons and refugees from Ukraine in one of the Creative Europe countries, veterans and vulnerable groups; submit a complete application form in either Ukrainian or English language. SELECTION CRITERIA AND PROCESS: Relevance of professional context – Does the applicant demonstrate a convincing role within their artistic, cultural, or cultural-community environment, and clearly explain the relevance of their engagement through artistic practice, cultural production, and/or culture-based community initiatives? Personal wellbeing relevance – Is the requested support clearly related to maintaining or strengthening the applicant's personal wellbeing and resilience at this stage of their life and work? Public and community impact – Is the applicant able to convincingly demonstrate their continued contribution to arts, culture, and/or culture-based community life, generating benefits for the communities, audiences, or cultural environments with which they engage? Coherence and feasibility of the planned use of funds - Are the requested activities realistic and eligible to the purpose of supporting the applicant's wellbeing? Following an eligibility check, applications will be assessed by external advisors who are familiar with the cultural sector and the current context in Ukraine. Final decisions will be made by the consortium partners, who review the recommendations to ensure consistency and budgetary balance. 7 to 10 applications will be awarded per round. budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Perform Europe is a funding scheme offering EUR 1.4 million for performing arts collaborations across all 41 Creative Europe countries. Perform Europe supports partnership proposals which reinvent the way we tour across borders. The highly successful Perform Europe pilot (2020–2022) and second edition (2023–2026), was coordinated by a Consortium of six organisations; five major performing arts networks, IETM - International network for contemporary performing arts, European Festivals Association (EFA), European Dance Development Network (EDN), Circostrada, Pearle* - Live Performance Europe together with the research organisation IDEA Consult. Co-funded by the European Union, Perform Europe has granted a total of €3.5 million to 61 cross-border macro-projects involving 272 partners. Together, they have toured over 80 artistic works across 41 countries, reaching new audiences and testing innovative approaches to inclusion, sustainability and cooperation. Building on these achievements, the third and final edition of Perform Europe under the current Creative Europe programme (2021-2028) will continue to explore, together with the performing arts sector, how cross-border touring can become fairer, greener and more inclusive, while further consolidating the knowledge, partnerships and practices developed through the programme. By the end of this third edition, Perform Europe will have supported at least 86 cross-border touring projects in total, building a substantial body of experience and knowledge that continues to strengthen the European performing arts ecosystem. Keywords: performing arts, theatre, dance, performance, circus, outdoor arts, puppetry, interdisciplinary, change-makers, inclusion, diversity, fight against climate change, sustainability, fairness, cross-border mobility, innovation Do you have an innovative idea that resonates with these keywords? Read on! PRIORITIES OF PERFORM EUROPE Proposals are submitted by collaboration partnerships of performing arts professionals and organisations. Partners should work on their proposal together. This is a call to the sector to create partnerships and propose impactful ideas that can generate real change via two main priorities: INCLUSION & DIVERSITY FIGHT AGAINST CLIMATE CHANGE Each proposal should choose one of the above main priorities to focus on, while still taking into account and implementing measures related to the second priority. In addition, all proposals should aim for quality and innovation, be built on fair practices, and are encouraged to promote collaboration across different regions within the 41 Creative Europe countries. Read more about the priorities in our guidelines below. CONDITIONS OF THE CALL The open call was launched on 23 June 2026. We invite you now to build partnerships, jointly develop proposals, and submit them through our website before 22 October 2026, 23:59 CEST. FUNDING Perform Europe will grant EUR 1.4 million to at least 25 partnerships . Partnerships can apply for grants in three categories: EUR 15,000 - small grant EUR 25,000 - medium grant EUR 55,000 - large grant In addition to the requested grant category, partnerships can request top-ups to address the sustainability and accessibility needs of their proposal. Each partnership may request any combination of the available top-ups, up to a maximum total top-up request of EUR 5,000 per proposal. The maximum granted amount, including top-ups, will be EUR 60,000, a requirement set by the funder, the European Union. Of the total funding, 5% will be allocated to proposals which involve a partnership with Ukrainian partners or support initiatives for the Ukrainian performing arts sector. WHO CAN APPLY Any organisation and professional working in the performing arts, and legally based in one of the Creative Europe Countries ( 27 EU member states plus 14 non-EU Participating Countries ). PARTNERSHIP REQUIREMENTS Proposals are submitted by partnerships. Each partnership must consist of a minimum of three partners from a minimum of three Creative Europe countries. Each proposal must include at least one performing arts work (excluding live music and opera) to be presented in a minimum of three different Creative Europe countries. Important to note: Perform Europe will not cover production costs for new creations: proposals are supposed to include a finished artistic work (finished production or an artistic concept ready to be applied and presented in different contexts). Looking for partners? Use the Matchmaking Platform on the Perform Europe website to join a community of over 2,300 performing arts organisations and professionals from 41 countries looking to make changes in the sector. TIMELINE 23 June 2026: Launch of the open call 22 October 2026 23:59 CEST: Deadline for submitting proposals January 2027: Announcement of selected partnerships 1 March 2027: Selected proposals start touring 31 January 2028: Selected proposals finish touring During the open call period, Perform Europe will organise help desk sessions, information, promotion and knowledge-sharing events regarding the open call. Check out the events calendar for more details. GET READY TO APPLY Read the full open call guidelines below Register and apply on the Perform Europe website Apply before Thursday, 22 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST APPLICATION DOCUMENTS Perform Europe Open Call and Guidelines PDF-version of the digital application form Budget template Cooperation agreement template Co-financing commitment letter template Frequently Asked Questions IMPORTANT RESOURCES Perform Europe Conversation Starter for building partnerships and designing your proposal Perform Europe Guidebook and Resources for inspiration and research Help Desk Sessions – for all your questions The Matchmaking Platform – for finding partners To stay updated about all events and important news, visit our website at performeurope.eu , subscribe to our newsletter and follow us on social media @PerformEurope.

title: Circulation of European literary works
description: Expected Impact: The action is expected to support around 40 projects, implemented either by a single entity (mono-beneficiary) or by a consortium of organisations (multi-beneficiary). Objective: This action will support projects that will translate, publish, distribute, and promote European Literature. This action complements the other Creative Europe support actions to the book and publishing sector, such as reading promotion through the European Authors Day to younger audiences and the European Union Prize for Literature targeting European emerging authors. The works covered by this call for proposals are European literary works , such as novels, short stories, theatre plays and radio plays, poetry, literary reportage, comic books as well as children and youth literature. For the purposes of this call for proposals ‘ European literary works’ refers to works written by authors who are linked to an eligible country (Creative Europe countries)[EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories (OCTs)) + non-EU countries: listed EEA countries and countries associated to the Creative Europe Programme ( list of participating countries )], by their nationality or place of residence, or who are recognised as belonging to the European literary heritage. Themes and priorities In line with the current cultural policy priorities, applicants should propose projects contributing to: 1. EU Overarching priorities: Applicants must describe in their application how, in the design and implementation of their projects, they intend to contribute to the EU's Overarching priorities. 2. The following specific priorities: Increasing the transnational circulation and the diversity of European literary works, notably through the translation, publication, distribution and promotion of works written in less translated languages; Promoting reading and the linguistic and cultural diversity of European literature to a large audience, through increasing discoverability of the literary works supported; Supporting the profession of literary translator, in line with the principles of good working conditions and fair remuneration publishers should ensure that the names of the translators appear visibly in published books, and preferably on the cover, and that the source language is also clearly mentioned; Increasing the competitiveness of the book sector by encouraging cooperation between different actors within the book value chain, notably between publishers, booksellers, and libraries. In addition, as part of the exceptional support to Ukraine, applicants are encouraged to propose activities facilitating the circulation of books from and/or into Ukraine, as well as their translation into or from Ukrainian. In addition, projects aimed at providing books in the Ukrainian language to Ukrainian refugees and displaced people will be encouraged. In this context, the printing in Ukrainian of (non-translated) Ukrainian books will be eligible. To support the profession of literary translator, in accordance with the principles of good working conditions and fair remuneration, it is recommended that between 20 and 30%[This percentage will apply to novel literary genre.] of the total project budget is allocated to the remuneration of translators and that translators are given recognition and visibility, particularly being credited, preferably on the cover page. To preserve the profession of literary translator, and the quality of translation, machine translation is excluded from this call. Publishers will have to sign contracts with professional human literary translators, and the data about the chosen translators must be clearly indicated in the overview of translations in the Creative Europe Database (see section 5. Admissibility and documents). In this regard, publishers should respect national standards and follow best practices, referring to and using, the ‘Translators on the cover’ report and, as an example, the ‘Guidelines for fair translation contracts’ drawn up by CEATL . Scope: Translation, publication, promotion, and distribution activities as well as activities addressing the themes and priorities described above. More specifically: Activities relating to literary works to be translated, published and promoted, as part of a robust publishing strategy and an effective distribution plan. Activities aimed at facilitating collaboration between the various stakeholders in the book and publishing value chain: authors, translators, publishers, distributors, booksellers, libraries, literary events and festivals. The proposed activities should be grouped, in the application form (part B), in coherent work packages. Each work package must have a corresponding list of activities, deliverables, milestones, and critical risks.

title: Audience Development and Film Education
description: Expected Impact: Stimulate interest and increase knowledge of audiences in European films, including specific programmes on film heritage, and other audiovisual works including videogames and immersive content Strengthen pan-European cooperation for innovative audience development and film education projects especially using new digital tools Increase pan-European impact and audience outreach Develop film education projects across European and non-European territories Scope: Projects ensuring pan-European cooperation and innovation, based on a robust needs’ analysis of audiences, especially targeting young audiences, using evidence-based strategies, aiming to: - increase interest in, knowledge of and access to audiences, in particular young ones, to European films including dedicated programmes on film heritage and other audiovisual works, - enhance pan-European impact and audience outreach, - promote and increase the contribution of existing European films and audiovisual works, towards audience development, film education and film literacy. Activities should include audience-oriented events and innovative or cross-border film education initiatives. Cooperation between film institutions and existing online platforms is encouraged. Applications should present a thorough analysis of audiences’ and/or markets’ needs, supported by solid evidence. The expected impacts on European audiences and the added value of the proposal’s activities must be clearly outlined, including quantifiable targets. Strategies must be presented to ensure a more sustainable and environmentally respectful industry along with ensuing gender balance, inclusion, diversity and representativeness. Projects are also encouraged to engage audiences in areas where cinema infrastructures are poorly developed (cinema deserts).

title: European co-development
description: Scope: The objective of the support to European co-development is to support the cooperation among European production companies that are developing works with a strong international audience potential. Expected results Increased collaboration at development stage between European production companies from different countries and from different markets and consequently an increased number of co-productions. Increased quality, feasibility, cross-border potential and market value of selected projects. A stronger position on European and international markets for companies selected under European co-development. Increased international cooperation, including collaborations between European and Korean professionals, in line with the audiovisual entitlement appended to the Protocol on Cultural Cooperation between the EU and Korea. Description of the activities to be funded The European co-development action shall provide support to the development of a single project for commercial exploitation intended for cinema release, television broadcasting or commercial exploitation on digital platforms or a multi-platform environment in the following categories: animation, creative documentary or fiction. The project must be co-developed by at least two European independent production companies, having signed a co-development agreement specifying the division of tasks and the collaboration on creative aspects. The aim is to provide funds to audiovisual production companies to develop works with high creative value and cultural diversity and wide cross-border exploitation potential. Companies are encouraged to develop strong and innovative collaborations at creative and financing level and to develop strategies for marketing and distribution from the outset of the development phase thus improving the potential to reach audiences at a European and international level. Applications should present adequate strategies to ensure a more sustainable and more environmentally-respectful industry and to ensure gender balance, inclusion, diversity and representativeness.

title: European slate development
description: Scope: The objective of the European slate development support is to foster the competitiveness of European independent production companies and to increase their economic weight on the market. The aim is also to increase the capacity of audiovisual producers to develop projects with the potential to circulate throughout Europe and beyond, and to facilitate European and international coproduction. The support will also provide an entry point for emerging talent, giving them the opportunity to direct a short film supported by the strong foundation provided by experienced companies. Expected results A stronger position on European and international markets for companies selected under European slate development. Increased quality, feasibility, cross-border potential and market value of European works supported. Description of the activities to be funded Support will be given to independent European production companies able to develop a slate of 3 to 5 audiovisual works (fiction, animation, creative documentary). This should allow production companies to reduce risks and increase their capacity to attract and retain talents. The European slate development shall provide support to the development of minimum 3 and maximum 5 works for commercial exploitation intended for cinema release, television broadcasting or commercial exploitation on digital platforms or a multi-platform environment in the following categories: animation, creative documentary or fiction. Applicants may add a short film by emerging talent to their slate (optional). The aim is to provide funds to audiovisual production companies to develop work with high creative value and cultural diversity and wide cross-border exploitation potential. Companies are encouraged to develop strategies for marketing and distribution from the outset of the development phase thus improving the potential to reach audiences at a European and international level. Greater cooperation, including co-development, between operators from different countries participating in the MEDIA Strand is also pursued as well as strengthening the competitiveness of European audiovisual production companies by consolidating their capacity for investment in the development phase and expanding companies’ activities and their innovation capacity to explore new fields and markets. Special attention will be given to applications presenting adequate strategies to ensure a more sustainable and more environmentally-respectful industry and to ensure gender balance, inclusion, diversity and representativeness.

title: European video games and immersive content
description: Scope: The objective of the support to Video games and immersive content development is to increase the capacity of European video game producers, XR studios and audiovisual production companies to develop video games and interactive immersive experiences with the potential to reach global audiences. The support also aims to improve the competiveness of the European video games industry and other companies producing interactive immersive content in European and international markets by enabling the retention of intellectual property by European developers. Expected results Increased quality, appeal, feasibility and cross-border potential for selected projects. A stronger position on the European and international market for video games developers and companies producing interactive immersive experiences. Description of the activities to be funded Support will be given to the development of works and prototypes of interactive narrative storytelling with original content and/or quality gameplay intended for production and global commercial exploitation via PCs, consoles, mobile devices, tablets, smart phones and other technologies. The aim is to provide funds to video game production companies and other companies producing immersive content to develop works with a high level of originality and innovative and creative value, and that have a high level of commercial ambition and extensive cross-border potential to reach European and international markets. This will allow for further investment in innovative European content and increase the competitiveness of European companies in the digital global market. Applications should present adequate strategies to ensure a more sustainable and more environmentally-respectful industry and to ensure gender balance, inclusion, diversity and representativeness.

title: TV and online content Animation projects
description: Scope: The objective of the support to TV and online content is to increase the capacity of audiovisual producers to develop and produce strong projects with significant potential to circulate throughout Europe and beyond, and to facilitate European and international co-productions within the television and online sector. The action aims to strengthen the independence of producers in relation to broadcasters and digital platforms, to enhance collaboration between operators, including independent producers, broadcasters, digital platforms and sales agents, from different countries participating in the MEDIA strand, including from low capacity countries, in order to produce high quality programming aimed at wide international distribution and promoted to a wide audience including commercial exploitation in the multi-platform environment. Particular attention will be given to projects presenting innovative aspects in the content and in the financing that show a clear link with the envisaged distribution strategies. Supported projects can also have associated partners from countries not participating in the MEDIA Strand, though these cannot be beneficiaries. These partners can come from non-European countries to foster wider international cooperation and market access: a case in point is Korea pursuant to the audiovisual entitlement appended to the Protocol on Cultural Cooperation between the EU and Korea. Expected results Increased production of high quality European works for linear and non-linear broadcasting including on digital platforms, as well as an increase in the number of co-productions. Enhanced cooperation between operators from different countries participating in the MEDIA Strand, including between broadcasters. Increased audience for European works through linear and non-linear broadcasting including on digital platforms. Increased international cooperation, including collaborations between European and Korean professionals, in line with the audiovisual entitlement appended to the Protocol on Cultural Cooperation between the EU and Korea. Description of the activities to be funded The TV and online content action supports works (drama films, animation and documentary) intended for linear and non-linear broadcasting, presenting: strong cooperation between operators from different countries participating in the MEDIA Strand, including between broadcasters; high creative/artistic value and wide cross-border exploitation potential able to reach audiences at European and international level; innovative aspects in terms of the content and the financing that show a clear link with the envisaged distribution strategies. Applicants should present adequate strategies to ensure a more sustainable and more environmentally-respectful industry (in particular through the use of greening consultants allowing to reduce the environmental impact of productions and shootings) and to ensure gender balance, inclusion, diversity and representativeness.

title: TV and online content Fiction projects
description: Scope: The objective of the support to TV and online content is to increase the capacity of audiovisual producers to develop and produce strong projects with significant potential to circulate throughout Europe and beyond, and to facilitate European and international co-productions within the television and online sector. The action aims to strengthen the independence of producers in relation to broadcasters and digital platforms, to enhance collaboration between operators, including independent producers, broadcasters, digital platforms and sales agents, from different countries participating in the MEDIA strand, including from low capacity countries, in order to produce high quality programming aimed at wide international distribution and promoted to a wide audience including commercial exploitation in the multi-platform environment. Particular attention will be given to projects presenting innovative aspects in the content and in the financing that show a clear link with the envisaged distribution strategies. Supported projects can also have associated partners from countries not participating in the MEDIA Strand, though these cannot be beneficiaries. These partners can come from non-European countries to foster wider international cooperation and market access: a case in point is Korea pursuant to the audiovisual entitlement appended to the Protocol on Cultural Cooperation between the EU and Korea. Expected results Increased production of high quality European works for linear and non-linear broadcasting including on digital platforms, as well as an increase in the number of co-productions. Enhanced cooperation between operators from different countries participating in the MEDIA Strand, including between broadcasters. Increased audience for European works through linear and non-linear broadcasting including on digital platforms. Increased international cooperation, including collaborations between European and Korean professionals, in line with the audiovisual entitlement appended to the Protocol on Cultural Cooperation between the EU and Korea. Description of the activities to be funded The TV and online content action supports works (drama films, animation and documentary) intended for linear and non-linear broadcasting, presenting: strong cooperation between operators from different countries participating in the MEDIA Strand, including between broadcasters; high creative/artistic value and wide cross-border exploitation potential able to reach audiences at European and international level; innovative aspects in terms of the content and the financing that show a clear link with the envisaged distribution strategies. Applicants should present adequate strategies to ensure a more sustainable and more environmentally-respectful industry (in particular through the use of greening consultants allowing to reduce the environmental impact of productions and shootings) and to ensure gender balance, inclusion, diversity and representativeness.
