title: Specialised education programmes in key capacity areas
description: The internship period must be in line with the objective of the Master : - a complete understanding on how AI is used in biomedical and healthcare research, - a better identification, a controlled development and validation of biomarkers used for prevention, diagnosis or monitoring diseases, - a more appropriate use of Information Technology tools and methods to analyse the data to exploit the full potential of large datasets from medical and biological research, - the latest AI operating techniques, such as machine learning and deep learning, to propose innovative solution in personalised medicine, - designing, planing and conducting high-impact research, - the participation in interdisciplinary research project involving skills in biology, AI and bio-informatics, by identifying specificlly required input from each main scientific area to come up with innovative solutions in the health field.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Purpose : Aix-Marseille Université is opening applications for granting and paying funds for the traineeship period of students enrolled in Master 2 « Biology & Health », study-track « Biomarkers and AI » at the Faculty of Medical & Paramedical Sciences. The hosting organism : The aim of the action is to provide the allocation required during the training period in work-placement by the French Law regarding traineeships lasting more than 2 months, which must be paid in the form of daily allowance for work-placement (4,35 €/ hours) for a actual working time not exceeding 10 hours per day. Legal working week cannot exceed 35 hours. The principles and procedure for awarding funding is granted through a list of internships, which are proposed in line with the thematic area of the programme AI and Health and its implementation. Combination with another European funded grant, such as the allowance awarded as part of the mobility for traineeship within the Programme Erasmus+ is not allowed, due to the question of possible double-funding. Participants must be EU citizens with a European nationality to be eligible for European funding under the project "Advanced Digital Skills AI and Health" . Applications : The student interested by an internship must be enrolled in Master 2 « Biology & Health », study-track « AI and biomarkers » at Aix-Marseille Université to acquire academic qualifications corresponding to this level. Applicants must send the following documents : the completed form and attachments, which must be returned by e-mail to Mrs Nicole Haroun : nicole.haroun@univ-amu.fr , project manager for the European project « AI and Health ». The attachments are a cover letter explaining the motivations to undertake an internship, a CV, the internship request form (the form of Aix-Marseille Université is available on the link : https://aiandhealth.eu/ ), proof of liability insurance, copy of the student card or certificate of enrolment at the university and ID card. Selection criteria : the choice of the location of the traineeship is the prevailing factor in deciding who gets the scholarship, depending on the location of the internship on the French mainland and oversea territories or in a third country not associated to the Programme Erasmus+. The decision of awarding the allowance is made on the basis of internship requirements, merit and individual qualifications of the student. Weight of evaluation criteria : 1.the thematic subject of the internship should be perfectly in line with the objective of the Master (3/5 points); 2.the great potential for publication in connection with the results achieved during the internship (1/5 points); 3.acquisition of new digital and technical skills (1/5 points). The applications of successful candidates are selected by representatives of the pedagogical team of the Master « Biology & Health », which comprises at least 3 members of the pedagogical team, including one representative from the Institut Laënnec.
furtherInformation:
Payment arrangements : the student is paid by Aix-Marseille Université, according to the time spent in the hosting organism and declared in the time sheet for work placement payment.

Maximum budget of this call : 210 000 euros

Amount of monthly allowance for the traineeship : between 487,20 euros (16 days) and 639,45 euros (20 days)

title: Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas
description: Purpose, amount and duration of the DIGISOC Scholarship The University of Innsbruck is issuing a Call for Application within the DIGISOC Scholarship Programme, reserved for students enrolled for the Academic Year 2026/2027 in the second year of the Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC). The Call for Application has a total budget of EUR 50.000. The DIGISOC Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the DIGISOC Joint Master’s Programme (JMP) and aims to: · Alleviate costs associated with tuition fees, summer schools, short-term mobilities, and living expenses; · Support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds; · Promote diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education. The scholarship also functions as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic obstacles that hinder participation in international education. The DIGISOC Scholarship is limited to one academic year and is paid out in one instalment. There is no automatic entitlement to a scholarship and no automatic renewal. The amount of the scholarship can reach a maximum of EUR 3,000.00 gross per academic year and applicant. The exact amount assigned to each applicant is based on the points awarded in the evaluation process (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure). A maximum of 30 points can be awarded to each application. The maximum total funding per student is EUR 6,000.00 over the course of the two-year programme. For the entire academic year for which the scholarship is awarded, the scholarship holder must not have an employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck. Applicants and scholarship holders are solely responsible for clarifying and complying with all tax obligations and any other individual tax consequences arising from receipt of the scholarship. The University of Innsbruck does not provide individual tax advice.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Eligibility Criteria Students enrolled in DIGISOC for the second year are eligible to apply for a scholarship if they meet one or more of the following criteria: 1. Students with certified disabilities Students with certified disabilities can apply for a DIGISOC scholarship. In the context of this call, and following Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, students with disabilities are considered students who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of a national disability status. 2. Migrants or refugees Students who are migrants or refugees can apply for funding based on their status. Required proof may include an asylum decision, a residence permit, or confirmation issued by a migration authority. 3. Students with low socio-economic family conditions Students from families with low socio-economic conditions can apply for funding. Low socio-economic conditions are defined according to the student’s family income. Required proof may include a tax statement, an income certificate, or an official social benefit statement. 4. Students living in remote areas Students living in a region in the lowest 25% of national population density and/or with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius may apply. Required proof is a residence certificate, which will be assessed against infrastructure data based on national statistics. Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027 The deadline to submit applications for the DIGISOC scholarships is 10. December 2026 at 23.59 CET (Central European Time). Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link: https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/114518610654144 Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labelled with the applicant’s name: · The signed Application Letter (Annex 1); · The applicant’s registration number (Matrikelnummer) at the University of Innsbruck; · The supporting documentation for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert. · The Data Protection and Consent Declaration (Annex 2). The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; documents in other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application. By submitting the application and signing Annex 1, the applicant expressly confirms that the application has been submitted completely and correctly and that all information and supporting documents are accurate and complete. Incomplete applications may be excluded from the selection procedure. Evaluation Committee A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Study Coordinator (Studienbeauftragter) of the Faculty of Economics and Statistics of the University of Innsbruck, reviews all applications and consists of: · One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree-awarding universities; · At least one student representative from the University of Innsbruck; · Disability officer at the University of Innsbruck. The Committee is appointed after the deadline for application submission and completes the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline. Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure The joint Evaluation Committee will evaluate each application and award points based on the following criteria: 1. Students with certified disabilities Applicants will be awarded points on the basis of the severity and impact of their condition, ranging from 5 points for a comparatively less impactful disability to 10 points for a very serious disability. 2. Migrants or refugees Applicants will be awarded points as follows: a. 10 points for refugee status; b. 10 points for migrant status with less than 5 years in the current country of residence; c. 5 points for migrant status with 5 or more years in the current country of residence. 3. Low socio-economic family condition Applicants will be awarded 10 points if their family income falls within the first quartile (Q1), i.e. within the 25% of the population with the lowest incomes in their country of origin. Applicants will be awarded 5 points if their family income falls between the first and second quartile (Q2), i.e. within the range defined by the median income and Q1 in their country of origin. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the year in which the application is submitted. 4. Remote areas Applicants will be awarded 5 points for residence in a remote area. An additional 5 points will be awarded if the student’s residence is in a remote area with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius. All applications will be ranked on the basis of the sum of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application can obtain a maximum of 30 points. To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use a proportional point-based model: · Total funds available are divided by the sum of all points awarded across valid applications; · This determines a value per point (EUR/point); · Each applicant receives funding according to their own score, up to the maximum of EUR 3,000.00. The decision of the joint Evaluation Committee is final, subject to the appeal procedure set out in Article 6. The exact amount of funding and its composition awarded to each applicant will be published via the Learning Management System OpenOLAT. This publication constitutes as notification.
furtherInformation:
Acceptance and Appeals

Applicants are notified of decisions within 15 days after the end of the submission period via e-mail. Rejected applications include a short justification.

Applicants who are not awarded a scholarship have the right to appeal. Appeals may be submitted by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at and will be reviewed by the joint Evaluation Committee, including the designated representative responsible for disability, inclusion and/or equal-treatment matters.

Within the mandatory deadline of 5 days from receipt of the scholarship award notice, the applicant must send the declaration of acceptance by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at without reservation and under the conditions of this Call for Application. Failure to do so results in forfeiture of the award.

With the declaration of acceptance, the scholarship holder must also undertake to communicate any change occurring during the academic year that affects information previously declared or eligibility for the scholarship.


Requirements for receiving the scholarship

Before disbursement, the scholarship holder will complete the required scholarship documentation with the University of Innsbruck and must provide:

·       A current enrolment certificate showing the register number;

·       The applicant’s full residential address (street and house number, postal code, city, and country);

·       Bank details for an account held in the scholarship holder’s name, including an IBAN and any further information required to enable a SEPA credit transfer. It must be expressly possible to make the scholarship payment by SEPA transfer to the account provided;

·       A copy of a valid passport or other accepted identification document.

Scholarship holders remain solely responsible for all tax-law clarifications and obligations connected with the scholarship.

The scholarship holder must also confirm that no employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck exists or will exist for the duration of the academic year for which the scholarship is awarded.


Financial and Disbursement Procedures

Scholarships are paid in one instalment per academic year. 

Disbursement is handled by the University of Innsbruck as the DIGISOC degree-awarding university issuing this Call for Application.

Payment will be made by SEPA credit transfer to a current account in the name of the scholarship holder. The account provided must be capable of receiving a SEPA transfer. The scholarship holder is responsible for providing complete and correct bank details and for any bank charges or conversion costs that may arise outside the scope of the SEPA payment.


Renunciation

In the event of withdrawal from the scholarship after acceptance, scholarship holders must give written notice by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at.

In case of transfer to another programme during the 2026/2027 academic year, the scholarship holder will be considered to have renounced the scholarship and must return the full amount of the scholarship.

A scholarship holder who renounces the scholarship is required to return any amounts received, except in duly justified special cases, which will be assessed by the joint Evaluation Committee.


Final provisions

All resources and updates will be made available via the DIGISOC website – Costs and Scholarships page https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/

The following templates and tools will be published on the same page:

·       Application and documentation guidelines;

·       Acceptance letter template.

For further questions, please contact:

·       Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II: digisoc@unina.it

·       Univerzita Palackého v Olomouci, Czechia: digisoc@upol.cz

·       University of Innsbruck, Austria: digisoc@uibk.ac.at


Disclaimer

This Call for Application and the financial support awarded under it do not constitute an EU action. The Call is launched and administered by the University of Innsbruck in its own name and under its own responsibility.

The scholarship programme is partially financed with funds made available to the University of Innsbruck in the framework of the EU-funded EURIDICE / DIGISOC project. Notwithstanding this source of funding, the financial support to successful applicants is awarded and provided directly by the University of Innsbruck. 

The University of Innsbruck remains responsible for the preparation and implementation of this Call, including the application procedure and the selection of successful applicants by the joint Evaluation Committee appointed in accordance with Article 4.

The publication of this Call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information and visibility purposes, including to inform potential applicants. Such publication does not imply any direct or indirect approval, endorsement or validation by the European Union or any of its institutions, bodies or agencies of the content, conditions, selection procedure or outcome of this Call. Nor does such publication transfer to the European Union any responsibility for the administration of the Call or the award of the scholarships, which remains with the University of Innsbruck.

title: Boosting Digital Skills of young pupils, in particular girls
description: The purpose of this call is to identify and support projects that can foster EU Code Week’s mission to promote coding, computational thinking, and digital skills across Europe. The aim is to identify projects that can achieve large-scale impact and deliver on key EU Code Week performance indicators within the project implementation period. Key tasks: Supporting the organisation of a large number of impactful coding, computational thinking, digital skills, and STEM activities; Increasing the number of activities registered on the EU Code Week platform; Reaching a large number of participants through local, regional, national, or cross-border activities; Increasing the participation of girls and young women in coding, digital skills, and STEM education; Supporting career-focused events that introduce students to educational and professional opportunities in STEM and digital fields; Supporting university visits and other activities that strengthen connections between schools, students, and higher-education institutions; Supporting activities and approaches that can be replicated or scaled beyond the project implementation period. Priority will be given to projects that can deliver a large number of activities to the EU Code Week platform and participants while maintaining educational quality and demonstrating clear and measurable impact.

eligibilityText: A selection committee comprising community stakeholders and representatives from the Code4Europe Consortium will evaluate proposals. Each proposal will be assessed based on four main criteria: presentation (clarity and completeness of the application), design congruity (relevance to EU Code Week priorities, coherence and feasibility of activities, and availability of professional and organisational resources), quality (the educational approach, alignment with core digital and literacy competencies, collaboration with local networks, and potential for replicability), and impact (engagement of diverse stakeholders, inclusion of different participant groups, and specific attention to involving girls and fostering STEM education). The evaluation process will be transparent and objective, with measures in place to avoid any conflicts of interest.

description: The procedure follows the principles of: transparency, equal treatment, confidentiality, absence of conflict of interest. Admissibility and eligibility checks precede scoring; only eligible applications will be scored. Eligible proposals are ranked by total score within the available budget. The final award decision is endorsed by POLI.design. All applicants will receive a written justification for the decision, with terms to appeal. Selected beneficiaries will be requested to sign a Financial Support Agreement specifying the supported activity, eligible costs, maximum amount, payment schedule and reporting obligations. Failure to sign within the indicated timeframe may lead to loss of the grant by the autonomous decision of POLI.design. Payments will be made by POLI.design, normally after participation in the activity and approval of the beneficiary report and cost statement. Details are provided in the individual Financial Support Agreement (including e.g. the possibility of small prefinancing in justified cases).
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The Call has 5 distinct cut-off dates . All submitted applications (for the two objectives/priorities) by each deadline will be evaluated jointly and awarded until funding resources are available. The AI4Gov-X consortium reserves the right of integrating the funding budget with an extra allocation, until twice the initially allocated amount. Applications will be possible electronically and exclusively managed through the GoodGrants TM platform ( https://polidesign.grantplatform.com/ ) by filling in a form and attaching the required documentation. Beneficiaries must be natural persons and as a precondition, be enrolled students in the MagiX master's course (for objectives/priorities 1 and 2) and/or (for objective/priority 1) in one or more of the AI4Gov-X extracurricular activities, strictly identified from the list published on the project's website, at this link: https://ai4gov-x.eu/extracurricular-activities/ . Please note that the list will be updated on a monthly basis while the Call is open. Additionally for objective/priority 2 only, beneficiaries must be unemployed people, able to document the existence of an internship contract with a host organisation from the public or private sector, residing in an eligible country for the Call (for a full list see Further information below). A same natural person holding the necessary requisites may apply to both objectives within the same cut-off date or within two distinct cut-off dates. However, he or she can receive the financial benefits of either objective/priority only once. Evaluation of received applications will be done by a special committee established at the Funding Body, POLI.design . Each application will be evaluated from the perspectives of admissibility, eligibility, and merit. For both priorities/objectives, admissibility conditions will be that an electronic application has been received on or before the latest cut-off date, completed in all its parts, and with all required attachments, exclusively through the GoodGrants TM platform. Incomplete applications or submitted by other means will be discarded and proposed for resubmission at the next cut-off date. To pass the admissibility check, all applicants must submit at least: - A signed application form, - Their CV in Europass format (see https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv ), - A motivation letter, specifically mentioning their employment status, - Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable), - Signed declarations (on conflict of interest, double funding, etc.) using the templates available on the GoodGrants TM platform. Applicants to priority/objective 1 must additionally submit: - A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course and/or in an extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, and - An indicative cost breakdown (travel, accommodation, fees, etc.). Applicants to priority/objective 2 must additionally submit: - A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course, - Copy of an internship contract, or equivalent legally binding agreement, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, showing the amount paid by the host organisation. All the above documentation must be provided in English language . Unofficial translations are allowed in case of submission of documents that are natively not in English, but the applicant will take the risk and bear the consequences of any misinterpretation during the evaluation process. For both priorities/objectives, eligibility conditions will be that - The applicants must be natural persons and nationals of an eligible country for the Call (see Further information below). - They must be enrolled in, or formally accepted into , the MagiX master's course and/or any of the extracurricular activities of AI4Gov-X (depending on the priority/objective) at the time of application. - They must not be subject to restrictive measures or other disqualifying conditions according to the EU or national legislation in their country. - They cannot receive double funding for the same operation. - They cannot be awarded twice under the same priority/objective. - They must not be in a situation of conflict of interest with POLI.design or any other AI4Gov-X partner. For priority/objective 2 only, a supplementary eligibility condition will be that - The applicants must be unemployed people documenting their enrollment in an internship programme at a host organisation residing in an eligible country (see Further information below). Eligible applications received until the same cut-off date will be scored using the following criteria (max. 100 points): Criterion Description Score Excellence and relevance Academic/professional background and relevance to AI4Gov-X topics 0–30 Motivation and expected impact Motivation, expected learning and career impact 0–25 Financial need Economic situation and justification of need 0–25 European added value Cross-border dimension, diversity contribution, EU public sector fit 0–20 No minimum thresholds or weighting will be applied. In case of equal scores, the following priority rules will be adopted, in the same order: - Applicants documenting their enrollment in (or acceptance into) both the MagiX master's course and at least one extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme (only for objective/priority 1); - Applicants coming from countries that are not full members of the AI4Gov-X consortium. - Applicants from regions with average income below 75% of the EU average. - Female applicants. The maximum financial support per beneficiary is: EUR 5 000 (for both priorities/objectives 1 and 2) The awarded amount for priority/objective 1 is calculated on the basis of: - Actual and justified travel costs, - Actual and justified accommodation costs, - Actual and documented registration/participation fees. as reported in the indicative cost breakdown (see above). The Selection Committee may cap specific cost items if considered excessive or not in line with typical market prices for the location and period. The awarded amount for priority/objective 2 is calculated on the basis of the stipend/salary received by the beneficiary, as documented in the internship contract, or equivalent agreement (see above). For the avoidance of any doubt, the reimbursement of travel and accommodation costs, or other types of cost, is also eligible provided it is explicitly mentioned in the internship contract, or equivalent agreement. For both priorities/objectives, eligible expenses are those realised after the date of submission of the respective application . The priority/objective 1 scheme reimburses up to 50% of total eligible costs, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 156. The priority/objective 2 scheme reimburses an equivalent amount to the one perceived by the intern, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 234.
furtherInformation:

description: Link to the published call .
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Fact-checkers are frequently the targets of attacks and harassment as they speak truth to power. The fact-checking community has been repeatedly harassed: individual fact-checkers and organisations have faced threats, vandalised offices, SLAPPs, and coordinated online hate campaigns designed to censor or cancel their work. In response, the consortium comprised of the European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN) , together with its members Faktograf, Pagella Politica, Fact Review, FactCheck Cyprus, and Greece Fact Check , has initiated a protection scheme with the support of the European Union. The primary aim of this scheme is to provide direct, rapid support to fact-checkers in need (e.g. due to online harassment campaigns, hacking attempts, vandalisation of office spaces, threats of physical violence, physical attacks, threats of imprisonment or lawsuits, SLAPPs). Those facing harassment or requiring assistance for their psychological, physical, online or legal safety may submit requests for support under this call. All submissions will be handled with the utmost security and processed as quickly as possible to provide aid to those affected. Support and Eligible Activities Fact-checking organisations can request support for the following: Psychological Support: counselling, burnout prevention, and specialised training. Please note that costs for general staff wellbeing not linked to a specific incident or harassment situation are not eligible. Legal Aid: defence against defamation, harassment, cyber and physical violence, SLAPP suits, copyright disputes, etc. Please note that legal costs related to commercial disputes, employment matters, or issues unrelated to fact-checking activities are not eligible. Safe Workspace: this may include installation of security systems, purchase or rental of security equipment, rental of a secure workspace, or costs to enable staff to work remotely during a period of risk. For fact-checkers, the workspace is understood as the reporting assignment itself and the physical space immediately surrounding it. Emergency Relocation: transport, temporary housing, crisis coordination for teams in danger, etc. Cybersecurity: upgrades for encryption, security tools, and risk assessments, etc. Please note that general IT infrastructure upgrades not linked to a specific security threat or incident are not eligible. Eligibility Criteria To be eligible for funding, applicants must meet the following requirements: Legal entity: applicants must be a legal entity, whether for-profit or non-profit. Certification: applicants must be EFCSN certified fact-checking organisations or fact-checking organisations that can demonstrate they respect in practice the European Code of Standards for Independent Fact-Checking Organisations. Location: organisations must be based in the European Union or DEP-associated countries (see this document for the most up-to-date list). Single applicants: this call is intended for single applicants, i.e. consortia of organisations cannot apply for this call. Budget, Funding, Payment Terms, Grant Duration Total Call Budget: €340,169 Maximum Grant Amount: €20,000 per support request; in exceptional cases (e.g. relocation of a large team), grants can be up to €40,000. Such requests must be reasoned in detail and must be approved by the EFCSN Governance Body in addition to the standard selection procedure outlined below. Funding Rate: 50% Form of Grant: lump sums Number of Grants: ~17 Payment Structure: 75% upon approval of request, 25% following the approval of the final report. Exact amount must be calculated using this template table. List of eligible costs: Direct costs must be directly related to the implementation of the requested support and fall under one of the following categories (although the examples below are not exhaustive): A. Psychological Support: costs related to mental health, wellbeing support, physical checkups related to long-lasting stress, including counselling sessions, burnout prevention activities, and specialised trauma training provided by qualified professionals. B. Legal Aid: costs related to legal support services, including legal counsel or lawyer fees, court or filing fees, legal document translation, notary services, and other directly related legal expenses. C. Physical Safety: costs related to ensuring the physical safety of staff or premises, including security system installation, security equipment purchase or rental, secure workspace rental, remote work setup costs, and related services. D. Emergency Relocation: costs related to urgent relocation and crisis response, including transport, temporary accommodation, crisis coordination services, subsistence costs during relocation, and related support. E. Cybersecurity: costs related to digital security and protection, including security software or tool licences, cybersecurity audits or risk assessments, secure hardware (e.g. encrypted devices), implementation and setup costs, and related services. Retroactive costs: if a grant is approved, costs are eligible from the time of application submission. Indirect / Administrative costs: these are capped at 10% of total direct costs. Max. Grant Duration: 12 months Rolling basis: this call is open on a rolling basis from 2 September 2026 until 31 May 2028 (or until funds are depleted). Selection Procedure The evaluation will be conducted in two steps: Phase 1: AI Processing. The application platform will automatically review submitted applications to ensure that all required information has been provided and that applicants meet the basic eligibility criteria. Phase 2: Expert Evaluation. Requests will be evaluated by the consortium experts based on need, urgency, regional vulnerability, and the applicant’s capacity to absorb the support. Consortium experts may request additional advice from a multidisciplinary group of experts, comprising the Protection Scheme Advisory Board, and escalate particularly delicate decisions to the EFCSN Governance Body. EFCSN will oversee the process, ensuring transparency, financial safeguards, and equitable distribution. Applications will be assessed against the award criteria outlined below. The evaluation is conducted in several steps, depending on the amount and urgency of the request, as shown in the image linked here. The main criteria for evaluating the requests are: Category Description Max. points Need Clear evidence of an acute operational or financial gap directly tied to the emergency situation. Financial statements and other documents may be requested as evidence. 10 Urgency Time-sensitive circumstances where delayed support would meaningfully worsen the outcome. 10 Regional Vulnerability Context of operating environment: political, economic, or press freedom constraints that amplify risk. 10 Absorptive Capacity Organisational ability to receive, manage, and account for the funds in a timely manner. 10 How to Apply and Timeline To apply, please submit your request through the application platform . Requests for urgent support will be processed within 48 hours; other requests will be processed within 5 working days. Reporting An outcome report (financial and narrative) is expected from all grant recipients. Transparency Notice This call has also been published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. Funding granted through this call will be disclosed on efcsn.com/funding-opportunities . Disclosure will cover the name of the receiving organisation, amount, and grant duration. NB! If a grant recipient operates in a high-risk environment or handles sensitive data, they may request that their identity remains confidential during the implementation phase and be disclosed after the end of the funding cycle. Questions? Please send questions about this call to grants@efcsn.com .

title: I4MS (phase 4) - uptake of digital game changers
description: PULSATE is a part of the Horizon 2020 programme called I4MS funded by the European Commission with the goal to accelerate the design, development and uptake of advanced digital technologies by the European Manufacturing industry to empower personalised products and to facilitate cost-effective small-scale production. One of these digitalization technologies that PULSATE project is focused on is Laser-Based Advanced & Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM). To boost and support the uptake, PULSATE will select and support end-users (Adopters) SMEs and Slightly bigger companies that are willing to implement Laser-Based Advanced & Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM) technologies into their environment. To enable this, PULSATE project brings together a strong consortium comprising six competence centres (AIMEN, FTMC, MTC, SINTEF, Fraunhofer and CEA) with high-level expertise in LBAAM and digitisation, the European Photonics Industry Consortium (EPIC) to support the acceleration of EU innovative scale-up initiatives, and two highly innovative SMEs (CLESGO & Fundingbox) to establish and support the Digital Agora platform, maintain a Marketplace of digital services and to manage the mechanisms of financial support to selected companies and the connection with DIHs across all Europe. Through the 2 nd Open Call for Adopters, PULSATE will select up to 18 Adopter SMEs/Slightly Bigger companies that represent high-potential business use cases for implementation of LBAAM technology in their processes, products and business models. Selected Adopters will take part in a 3-month support programme between january and april 2024, through which they will receive: - Up to €25 000 as a lump sum - Mentorship from PULSATE Consortium partners in LBAAM feasibility assessment that will allow Adopters to confirm Technical and Business Feasibility for the implementation of LBBAM technology in their environment.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Applications must be submitted via https://pulsate-adopters.fundingbox.com . The selection of the open call proposals will be carried out in a four-step process: Step 1 will check the proposals against eligibility criteria. Step 2 will involve external evaluation to assess the proposal according to the criteria. Step 3 will involve the PULSATE consortium to prioritise the proposals based on the external evaluation results and the objectives of the PULSATE project. Step 4 legal check before finalists are invited to sign the Sub Grant Agreement. For further information see the Guide for Applicants section 4. Applicants eligibility PULSATE is looking for End-user / Technology Adopter companies that are interested in the implementation of LBAAM technology into their environment that will enhance the activities of the manufacturing industry. Adopters should represent high-potential business Use Cases for implementation of Laser-Based Advanced and Additive Manufacturing (LBAAM) technology in their processes, products and business models. Applications can be submitted by only ONE company that has the status of SMEs or a Slightly Bigger company and is legally established in one of the eligible countries. For further information see the Guide for Applicants section 3.

title: Ammunition, missiles and other explosive weapons
description: Expected Impact: The results of the activities should contribute to support common procurement, leading to strengthening the cooperation among Member States and associated countries, as well as to greater interoperability. Furthermore, they should contribute to the building up of strategic stockpile of ammunition, missiles, including their components, or to the increase of existing ones, as well as to the development of low-cost unmanned systems for guided strikes adapted to modern warfare scenarios. Objective: This topic aims at actions supporting the common procurement of ammunition (including small arms ammunition, tank and anti-tank ammunitions, artillery ammunition, guided ammunitions), missiles (all types of missiles) and other explosive weapons (including hand grenade, land and naval mines, mortar, rockets, unmanned systems (aerial, ground, surface and underwater vehicles controlled remotely or operating autonomously using advanced software and sensors) able to perform guided strikes (including attack or kamikaze drones, FPV loitering munitions), torpedoes), or parts thereof, contributing to replenishment of stocks. Scope: Common procurement actions under this topic shall consist of activities related to the cooperation of legal entities in the procurement of ammunition, missiles, and other explosive weapons, at any point in the life cycle of such defence products, including for the purpose of establishing, managing and maintaining defence industrial readiness pools. Where relevant (e.g. unmanned systems for guided strikes), procurement contracts are expected to include provisions allowing to rapidly upgrade the procured systems based on evolving lessons identified from the battlefield. To achieve the expected impact, the estimated value of a common procurement proposed for actions under this topic shall be of at least EUR 20 000 000 aiming to commonly procure defence products to fill the capability gaps and reinforce cooperation among Member States and associated countries. The procurement shall be based on a binding agreement to be signed by the participating Member States and associated countries with a procurement agent appointed by those Member States and associated countries. Such procurement agent may be contracting authorities of Member States or associated countries, the European Defence Agency (EDA), a Structure for European Armament Programme (SEAP) or other international organisation, including the Organisation for Joint Armament Cooperation (OCCAR) or the NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA). The cooperation shall be newly created in the context of the application to the call topic or based on an existing framework, provided that the activities under such cooperation framework did not start before 5 March 2024 and have not been completed before the signature of the grant agreement. Eligible actions are common procurement of systems, parts thereof or variants of systems. The common procurement can be organised as a framework contract. Actions shall be completed no later than 31 December 2033.

title: Erasmus Charter for Higher Education
description: Expected Outcome: This Call aims at accrediting recognised Higher Education Institutions located in eligible countries, which have operational capacity to take part in Erasmus+ Programme’s activities, such as learning mobility of individuals and/or cooperation for innovation and good practices. There is only ONE TOPIC. NO LIGHT PROCEDURE any longer. Therefore, ALL PARTS of the APPLICATION FORM PART B should be filled in. HEIs are reminded to use their existing PIC or create a new one if necessary. It is important to ensure that the organisational data under the used PIC to apply is up to date (e.g. address, legal information, etc.). Please note that OIDs cannot be used. Eligible applicants In order to be eligible, the applicants must: be higher education institution (HEI) (public or private) and be established in one of the eligible countries, i.e.: Erasmus+ Programme Countries: - EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories (OCTs)) Non-EU countries: - Listed EEA (European Economic Area) countries and countries associated to the Erasmus+ Programme (associated countries) or countries which are in ongoing negotiations for an association agreement, in particular Switzerland and United Kingdom (see below). - Western Balkans third countries not associated to the Erasmus+ Programme: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo and Montenegro. All applicants must register in the Participant Register — before the call deadline. Specific cases and definitions Higher education institutions (HEIs) — are institutions which offer recognised degrees or other tertiary level qualifications and other comparable institutions at tertiary level, if recognised by the national authorities. The applicant must be recognised as higher education institution by the national authority of its country. After closure of the call, the national authorities will be asked by EACEA to confirm that they are recognised in their countries. Switzerland, the United Kingdom and other countries currently negotiating association agreements - where an applicant established in Switzerland, the United Kingdom - or in other countries currently negotiating association agreements - is awarded the ECHE under this call, the validity of the ECHE is conditional upon and will only commence on the date when Switzerland, the United Kingdom - or other countries currently negotiating association agreements - officially becomes a third country associated to the Programme according to the Article 19 of the Erasmus+ Regulation 2021/817. Deadline for the submission of applications and indicative date for selection results Please check the call document for yearly deadlines.

title: ERC Consolidator Grant
description: Scope: Objectives The Consolidator Grant supports excellent Principal Investigators who are consolidating their own independent research team or programme. A Consolidator Grant Principal Investigator should have already shown evidence of research independence. Size of ERC Consolidator Grants Consolidator Grants may be awarded up to a maximum of EUR 2 000 000 for a period of 60 months . The maximum amount of the grants is reduced pro rata temporis for proposals of shorter duration. Additional funding up to EUR 1 000 000 *1 can be requested to cover further eligible costs for any cost category when these are necessary to carry out the proposed work. The request for additional funding must be duly justified in the proposal. The maximum amount of the grant is reduced pro rata temporis for proposals of shorter duration. Additional funding is not subject to pro rata temporis reduction for projects of shorter duration. Both the grant amount and any additional funding requested are assessed during evaluation. *1 Except for Principal Investigators in Starting, Consolidator, or Advanced Grant re-locating to the EU or an Associated Country from elsewhere to take up their ERC grant. In this case, the maximum additional funding shall be EUR 2 000 000. Applicants requesting more than EUR 1 000 000 as additional funding must be based outside the EU or an Associated Country at the time of the call deadline for the increased maximum additional funding to apply. Profile of the ERC Consolidator Grant Principal Investigator The Principal Investigators will be eligible for a Consolidator Grant if they have defended their PhD in the five to fifteen-year period preceding the 1st of January 2027. Cut-off dates: Successful defence of PhD between 1 January 2012 and 31 December 2021 (inclusive) * 2 . Principal Investigators who have already held a Starting or a Consolidator Grant in the past will not be able to apply for the same type of grant. Other eligibility or resubmission criteria might also apply. The eligibility period may be extended beyond 15 years in some well-documented circumstances or events. See section 1.4 Admissibility, Eligibility, Resubmission Restrictions of the ERC Work Programme 2027 . *2 A Principal Investigator applying for an ERC Starting or Consolidator Grant must hold a PhD or an equivalent doctoral degree at the time of the call deadline.

eligibilityText: "> General conditions 1. Admissibility conditions The conditions specific to ERC grants are described in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 1.4 'Admissibility, Eligibility, Resubmission Restrictions' and in the ERC Rules of Submission . An overview is provided below: Admissibility: A proposal must be complete (including all sections under 1.5 'Proposal Submission and Description' section), readable and, accessible. It must be submitted electronically by a Principal Investigator fulfilling the eligibility criteria ( section 1.4.2.2 'Eligible Principal Investigator(s)' ) before the respective call deadline. The proposal must also satisfy the requirements set out in the documents referenced in the call for proposals. The Host Institution must confirm its association with, and its support to, the project and the Principal Investigator through a binding statement of support ( i.e . the Host Institution Support Letter [ 1 ] ). This statement must be provided at the time of application. [1] A template of the letter is annexed to the Information for Applicants document for the respective call: Information for Applicants to the Starting and Consolidator Grant Calls , Information for Applicants to the Advanced Grant Call , Information for Applicants to the ERC Plus Call , Information for Applicants to the Synergy Grant Call . 2. Eligibility The content of the proposal must relate to the objectives and to the grant type set out in the call, as defined in the ERC Work Programme 2027 (section 1.1 ‘Objectives of ERC Grant Schemes’ ). If a proposal is considered not to relate to the objectives of the grant or call for proposals, it will be declared ineligible. Eligible Principal Investigators: The ERC grant schemes are open to researchers of any age and nationality, residing anywhere in the world at the time of application (except those subject to restrictions outlined in Annex 3 of the ERC Work Programme 2027 ), and wishing to carry out their research in one of the EU or Associated Country-based Host Institutions. Principal Investigators applying to the SConsolidator Grant must meet specific eligibility criteria based on the time elapsed between the date of the successful defence of their first PhD degree or an equivalent doctoral degree and the cut-off date specified in the ERC Work Programme 2027 . A Principal Investigator applying for an ERC Consolidtaor Grant must hold a PhD or an equivalent doctoral degree (for more information, including specific provisions for holders of medical degrees, see Annex 2 ). The Principal Investigators will be eligible for a Consolidator Grant if they have defended their PhD in the 5 to 15-year period preceding the 1st of January 2027. Cut-off dates: Successful defence of PhD between 1 January 2012 and 31 December 2021 (inclusive). All Principal Investigators funded through an ERC Consolidator Grant must spend a minimum of 40% of their working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and a minimum of 50% of their working time on the ERC project. Eligible Host Institution: Any type of legal entity, public or private, including a university, a research organisation or an undertaking can host a Principal Investigator and their team. To participate in ERC frontier research actions the Host Institution must be established either in an EU Member State or an Associated Country (see Annex 3 of the ERC Work Programme 2027 ) as a legal entity created under national law, or it may be an international European research organisation (such as CERN, EMBL, etc.), or any other entity created under EU law. International organisations with headquarters in an EU Member State or an Associated Country shall be deemed to be established in that Member State or Associated Country. Eligible countries: The conditions specific to the ERC are described in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 1 .4 ‘Admissibility, Eligibility, Resubmission Restrictions' and in Annex 3 . An overview is provided below: ERC grant schemes are open to researchers of any age and nationality, residing anywhere in the world at the time of application (except those subject to restrictions outlined in see Annex 3 of the ERC Work Programme 2027 ), and wishing to carry out their research in one of the EU Member State or Associated Country-based Host Institutions. Eligible Scientific Field: Applications in any field of science are eligible for the ERC funding and the ERC welcomes research proposals of an interdisciplinary nature. Restrictions on applications: Given the large number of applications received every year, and the need to uphold the quality and integrity of the evaluation process, restrictions apply to the ERC main grant calls. For further details please consult the ERC Work Programme 2027 , section 1.4.3 'Restrictions on applications’ and the corresponding Table 6 or the Frequently Asked Questions . 3. Proposal submission and description Complete proposals must be submitted via the submission tool available through the Funding & Tenders Portal (to access the submission tool, you need to register first). More information can be found in the ERC Information for Applicants and in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the section 1.5.1 ‘Proposal Description’. A proposal shall include the following sections: · The Administrative form Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table and the Budget Section ) is available in the submission tool below. The budget table and the justification of the Resources are part of this online form Part A (section 'Budget' ). For more details, please refer to section 2.2 ‘The Administrative Form’ of the ERC Information for Applicants . · Parts B ( Part I, Part II) and the Host Institution Support Letter templates are provided in the submission system as word-templates (they should be completed, uploaded and submitted via the submission tool as PDF files). For more details, please refer to section 2.3 ‘The Research Proposal’ of the ERC Information for Applicants . A complete proposal consists of the following elements (with the following page limits): · Part I of the Scientific Proposal: up to 5 pages. · Part II of the Scientific Proposal: up to 7 pages. · Curriculum Vitae and Track Record : up to 4 pages. · Resources and Time Commitment : up to 2 pages. · Host Institution Support Letter. · Ethics Issues Table. · PhD record and supporting documents for eligibility checking. 4. Financial and operational capacity and exclusion Financial capacity: Please refer to the ERC Rules of Submission and Evaluation under Horizon Europe, section 4, ‘A ward Decision and Preparation of Grant Agreements’ . Operational capacity: As indicated in the ERC Work Programme 2027 : An applicant whose proposal is marked above the 80% quality threshold is deemed to fulfil the operational capacity requirements of Article 201(3) of the EU Financial Regulation . Exclusion: Please refer to the ERC Work Programme 2027 , section ‘Prior Information of Candidates, Tenderers, Grant Applicants, and Remunerated Experts: registration of information in the Early Detection and Exclusion System (EDES)’: Applicants that are subject to the administrative sanction of exclusion or are in one of the exclusion situations set out by the EU Financial Regulation are banned from receiving EU grants and CANNOT participate. 5. Evaluation The conditions specific to ERC are described in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 1.6 ' Evaluation criterion, elements and procedure’ and in the ERC Rules of Submission , section 3.6 ‘The evaluation of ERC grants’. An overview is provided below: Evaluation criteria For all the main grants, excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation . The panels will primarily evaluate: the ground-breaking nature and ambition of the research project and, at the same time, the intellectual capacity and creativity of the Principal Investigator, with a focus on the extent to which the PI has the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project. The detailed evaluation elements applying to the excellence of the research project and the Principal Investigator are set out in the ERC Work Programme 2027 . Evaluation procedure The proposal is evaluated in two steps with interviews taking place at Step 2. The evaluation is carried out by peer review panels as listed in Annex 1 of the ERC Work Programme 2027 . The panels may be assisted by independent external experts working remotely. Evaluation Outcome At the end of Step 1 of the evaluation, each proposal receives one of the following scores: · A invited: the proposal is of excellent quality and ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation. · A not invited : the proposal is of excellent quality but not ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation. · B: the proposal is of high quality but not sufficient to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation. · C : the proposal is not of sufficient quality to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation. General conditions

1. Admissibility conditions

The conditions specific to ERC grants are described in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 1.4 'Admissibility, Eligibility, Resubmission Restrictions' and in the ERC Rules of Submission. An overview is provided below:

Admissibility: A proposal must be complete (including all sections under 1.5 'Proposal Submission and Description' section), readable and, accessible. It must be submitted electronically by a Principal Investigator fulfilling the eligibility criteria (section 1.4.2.2 'Eligible Principal Investigator(s)') before the respective call deadline. The proposal must also satisfy the requirements set out in the documents referenced in the call for proposals.

The Host Institution must confirm its association with, and its support to, the project and the Principal Investigator through a binding statement of support (i.e. the Host Institution Support Letter[1]). This statement must be provided at the time of application.

[1] A template of the letter is annexed to the Information for Applicants document for the respective call: Information for Applicants to the Starting and Consolidator Grant Calls, Information for Applicants to the Advanced Grant Call, Information for Applicants to the ERC Plus Call, Information for Applicants to the Synergy Grant Call.

2. Eligibility

The content of the proposal must relate to the objectives and to the grant type set out in the call, as defined in the ERC Work Programme 2027 (section 1.1 ‘Objectives of ERC Grant Schemes’). If a proposal is considered not to relate to the objectives of the grant or call for proposals, it will be declared ineligible.

Eligible Principal Investigators: The ERC grant schemes are open to researchers of any age and nationality, residing anywhere in the world at the time of application (except those subject to restrictions outlined in Annex 3 of the ERC Work Programme 2027), and wishing to carry out their research in one of the EU or Associated Country-based Host Institutions.

Principal Investigators applying to the SConsolidator Grant must meet specific eligibility criteria based on the time elapsed between the date of the successful defence of their first PhD degree or an equivalent doctoral degree and the cut-off date specified in the ERC Work Programme 2027. A Principal Investigator applying for an ERC Consolidtaor Grant must hold a PhD or an equivalent doctoral degree (for more information, including specific provisions for holders of medical degrees, see Annex 2).

The Principal Investigators will be eligible for a Consolidator Grant if they have defended their PhD in the 5 to 15-year period preceding the 1st of January 2027. Cut-off dates: Successful defence of PhD between 1 January 2012 and 31 December 2021 (inclusive).

All Principal Investigators funded through an ERC Consolidator Grant must spend a minimum of 40% of their working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and a minimum of 50% of their working time on the ERC project.

Eligible Host Institution: Any type of legal entity, public or private, including a university, a research organisation or an undertaking can host a Principal Investigator and their team. To participate in ERC frontier research actions the Host Institution must be established either in an EU Member State or an Associated Country (see Annex 3 of the ERC Work Programme 2027) as a legal entity created under national law, or it may be an international European research organisation (such as CERN, EMBL, etc.), or any other entity created under EU law. International organisations with headquarters in an EU Member State or an Associated Country shall be deemed to be established in that Member State or Associated Country.

Eligible countries:

The conditions specific to the ERC are described in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 1.4 ‘Admissibility, Eligibility, Resubmission Restrictions' and in Annex 3. An overview is provided below:

ERC grant schemes are open to researchers of any age and nationality, residing anywhere in the world at the time of application (except those subject to restrictions outlined in see Annex 3 of the ERC Work Programme 2027), and wishing to carry out their research in one of the EU Member State or Associated Country-based Host Institutions.

Eligible Scientific Field: Applications in any field of science are eligible for the ERC funding and the ERC welcomes research proposals of an interdisciplinary nature.

Restrictions on applications: Given the large number of applications received every year, and the need to uphold the quality and integrity of the evaluation process, restrictions apply to the ERC main grant calls. For further details please consult the ERC Work Programme 2027, section 1.4.3 'Restrictions on applications’ and the corresponding Table 6 or the Frequently Asked Questions.

3. Proposal submission and description

Complete proposals must be submitted via the submission tool available through the Funding & Tenders Portal (to access the submission tool, you need to register first). More information can be found in the ERC Information for Applicants and in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the section 1.5.1 ‘Proposal Description’.

A proposal shall include the following sections:

· The Administrative form Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table and the Budget Section) is available in the submission tool below. The budget table and the justification of the Resources are part of this online form Part A (section 'Budget'). For more details, please refer to section 2.2 ‘The Administrative Form’ of the ERC Information for Applicants.

· Parts B (Part I, Part II) and the Host Institution Support Letter templates are provided in the submission system as word-templates (they should be completed, uploaded and submitted via the submission tool as PDF files). For more details, please refer to section 2.3 ‘The Research Proposal’ of the ERC Information for Applicants.

A complete proposal consists of the following elements (with the following page limits):

· Part I of the Scientific Proposal: up to 5 pages.

· Part II of the Scientific Proposal: up to 7 pages.

· Curriculum Vitae and Track Record: up to 4 pages.

· Resources and Time Commitment: up to 2 pages.

· Host Institution Support Letter.

· Ethics Issues Table.

· PhD record and supporting documents for eligibility checking.

4. Financial and operational capacity and exclusion

Financial capacity: Please refer to the ERC Rules of Submission and Evaluation under Horizon Europe, section 4, ‘Award Decision and Preparation of Grant Agreements’.

Operational capacity: As indicated in the ERC Work Programme 2027: An applicant whose proposal is marked above the 80% quality threshold is deemed to fulfil the operational capacity requirements of Article 201(3) of the EU Financial Regulation.

Exclusion: Please refer to the ERC Work Programme 2027, section ‘Prior Information of Candidates, Tenderers, Grant Applicants, and Remunerated Experts: registration of information in the Early Detection and Exclusion System (EDES)’: Applicants that are subject to the administrative sanction of exclusion or are in one of the exclusion situations set out by the EU Financial Regulation are banned from receiving EU grants and CANNOT participate.

5. Evaluation

The conditions specific to ERC are described in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 1.6 'Evaluation criterion, elements and procedure’ and in the ERC Rules of Submission, section 3.6 ‘The evaluation of ERC grants’. An overview is provided below:

Evaluation criteria

For all the main grants, excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation. The panels will primarily evaluate: the ground-breaking nature and ambition of the research project and, at the same time, the intellectual capacity and creativity of the Principal Investigator, with a focus on the extent to which the PI has the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project. The detailed evaluation elements applying to the excellence of the research project and the Principal Investigator are set out in the ERC Work Programme 2027.

Evaluation procedure

The proposal is evaluated in two steps with interviews taking place at Step 2. The evaluation is carried out by peer review panels as listed in Annex 1 of the ERC Work Programme 2027. The panels may be assisted by independent external experts working remotely.

Evaluation Outcome

At the end of Step 1 of the evaluation, each proposal receives one of the following scores:

· A invited: the proposal is of excellent quality and ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation.

· A not invited: the proposal is of excellent quality but not ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation.

· B: the proposal is of high quality but not sufficient to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation.

· C: the proposal is not of sufficient quality to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation.

At the end of Step 2 of the evaluation, the proposal receives one of the following scores:

A: the proposal fully meets the excellence criterion and is recommended for funding should sufficient funds be available.

B: the proposal meets some but not all elements of the excellence criterion and will not be funded.

Indicative timeline for evaluation and grant agreement

Please refer to the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 'Table 1: Provisional Details on the Main Calls for Proposals under Work Programme 2027’.

6. Legal and financial set-up of the grants

During the grant preparation stage, the beneficiary will be asked to prepare the Grant Agreement, together with the EU project officer. This Grant Agreement will set out the framework for the grant and its terms and conditions, particularly concerning deliverables, reporting and payments. The applicable model with the complete text of the provisions is available on the topic page, together with the other call documentation.

Please refer to the MGA used for ERC actions under Horizon Europe (HE General MGA).

7. Open Science

Under Horizon Europe, all beneficiaries (including those of ERC grants) must ensure immediate open access to all peer-reviewed scientific publications relating to their results as set out in the Annex 5 of the applicable Model Grant Agreement used for ERC actions. Open access must be provided with full re-use rights. Beneficiaries must ensure that they or the authors retain sufficient intellectual property rights to comply with their open access requirements and the Grant Agreement obligations. Publishing costs can be considered as eligible costs provided that the publishing venue (e.g., journal, book) is fully open access.

In addition, beneficiaries of ERC grants funded under this Work Programme will be covered by the provisions on research data management as set out in the Model Grant Agreement used for ERC actions. In particular, whenever a project generates research data, beneficiaries are required to manage it in line with the principles of findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability as described by the FAIR principles’ initiative, and establish a data management plan within the first six months of project implementation. Open access to research data should be ensured under the principle ‘as open as possible, as closed as necessary’. These provisions are designed to facilitate access, re-use and preservation of the research data generated during the ERC funded research work.

title: ERC Starting Grant
description: Scope: Objectives The Starting Grant supports excellent Principal Investigators starting or having recently started their own independent research team or programme. A Starting Grant Principal Investigator should have already shown evidence of the potential for research independence, for example, by having produced at least one important publication as its main author or a publication without the participation of their PhD supervisor. A researcher may be the Principal Investigator of only one ERC Starting Grant in their career. Size of ERC Starting Grants Starting Grants may be awarded up to a maximum of EUR 1 500 000 for a period of 60 months . The maximum amount of the grants is reduced pro rata temporis for proposals of shorter duration. Additional funding up to EUR 1 000 000 *1 can be requested to cover further eligible costs for any cost category when these are necessary to carry out the proposed work. The request for additional funding must be duly justified in the proposal. The maximum amount of the grant is reduced pro rata temporis for proposals of shorter duration. Additional funding is not subject to pro rata temporis reduction for projects of shorter duration. Both the grant amount and any additional funding requested are assessed during evaluation. *1 Except for Principal Investigators in Starting, Consolidator, or Advanced Grant re-locating to the EU or an Associated Country from elsewhere to take up their ERC grant. In this case, the maximum additional funding shall be EUR 2 000 000. Applicants requesting more than EUR 1 000 000 as additional funding must be based outside the EU or an Associated Country at the time of the call deadline for the increased maximum additional funding to apply. Profile of the ERC Starting Grant Principal Investigator The Principal Investigators will be eligible for a Starting Grant if they have defended their PhD in the ten-year period preceding the 1st of January 2027. Cut-off dates: Successful defence of PhD between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2026 (inclusive) * 2 . Principal Investigators who have already held a Starting or a Consolidator Grant in the past will not be able to apply for the same type of grant. Other eligibility or resubmission criteria might also apply. The eligibility period may be extended beyond 10 years in some well-documented circumstances or events. See section 1.4 Admissibility, Eligibility, Resubmission Restrictions of the ERC Work Programme 2027 . *2 A Principal Investigator applying for an ERC Starting or Consolidator Grant must hold a PhD or an equivalent doctoral degree at the time of the call deadline.

Exclusion: Please refer to the ERC Work Programme 2027, section ‘Prior Information of Candidates, Tenderers, Grant Applicants, and Remunerated Experts: registration of information in the Early Detection and Exclusion System (EDES)’: Applicants that are subject to the administrative sanction of exclusion or are in one of the exclusion situations set out by the EU Financial Regulation are banned from receiving EU grants and CANNOT participate.

5. Evaluation

The conditions specific to ERC are described in the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 1.6 'Evaluation criterion, elements and procedure’ and in the ERC Rules of Submission, section 3.6 ‘The evaluation of ERC grants’. An overview is provided below:

Evaluation criteria

For all the main grants, excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation. The panels will primarily evaluate: the ground-breaking nature and ambition of the research project and, at the same time, the intellectual capacity and creativity of the Principal Investigator, with a focus on the extent to which the PI has the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project. The detailed evaluation elements applying to the excellence of the research project and the Principal Investigator are set out in the ERC Work Programme 2027.

Evaluation procedure

The proposal is evaluated in two steps with interviews taking place at Step 2. The evaluation is carried out by peer review panels as listed in Annex 1 of the ERC Work Programme 2027. The panels may be assisted by independent external experts working remotely.

Evaluation Outcome

At the end of Step 1 of the evaluation, each proposal receives one of the following scores:

· A invited: the proposal is of excellent quality and ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation.

· A not invited: the proposal is of excellent quality but not ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation.

· B: the proposal is of high quality but not sufficient to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation.

· C: the proposal is not of sufficient quality to pass to Step 2 of the evaluation.

At the end of Step 2 of the evaluation, the proposal receives one of the following scores:

A: the proposal fully meets the excellence criterion and is recommended for funding should sufficient funds be available.

B: the proposal meets some but not all elements of the excellence criterion and will not be funded.

Indicative timeline for evaluation and grant agreement:

Please refer to the ERC Work Programme 2027 under the heading 'Table 1: Provisional Details on the Main Calls for Proposals under Work Programme 2027’.

6. Legal and financial set-up of the grants

During the grant preparation stage, the beneficiary will be asked to prepare the Grant Agreement, together with the EU project officer. This Grant Agreement will set out the framework for the grant and its terms and conditions, particularly concerning deliverables, reporting and payments. The applicable model with the complete text of the provisions is available on the topic page, together with the other call documentation.

Please refer to the MGA used for ERC actions under Horizon Europe (HE General MGA).

7. Open Science

Under Horizon Europe, all beneficiaries (including those of ERC grants) must ensure immediate open access to all peer-reviewed scientific publications relating to their results as set out in the Annex 5 of the applicable Model Grant Agreement used for ERC actions. Open access must be provided with full re-use rights. Beneficiaries must ensure that they or the authors retain sufficient intellectual property rights to comply with their open access requirements and the Grant Agreement obligations. Publishing costs can be considered as eligible costs provided that the publishing venue (e.g., journal, book) is fully open access.

In addition, beneficiaries of ERC grants funded under this Work Programme will be covered by the provisions on research data management as set out in the Model Grant Agreement used for ERC actions. In particular, whenever a project generates research data, beneficiaries are required to manage it in line with the principles of findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability as described by the FAIR principles’ initiative, and establish a data management plan within the first six months of project implementation. Open access to research data should be ensured under the principle ‘as open as possible, as closed as necessary’. These provisions are designed to facilitate access, re-use and preservation of the research data generated during the ERC funded research work.

title: Structured dialogue with people with lived experience of poverty
description: Expected Outcome: The primary aim of this action is to create the conditions for a sustained dialogue between policymakers and individuals with lived experience of poverty, ensuring that those directly affected by poverty and/or social exclusion have a real and influential voice in the decisions that shape their lives. A core objective is to empower participants by providing them with the tools, confidence, and platforms needed to engage effectively in discussions on challenges related to combating poverty and social inclusion. This will come together with building trust and breaking down barriers between institutions and marginalised communities. The action will create a more inclusive and respectful exchange , where power imbalances are acknowledged and mitigated giving participants a clearer understanding of how policies are formed. Finally, the action will champion intersectionality : efforts will be made to amplify the voices of the most marginalised groups, ensuring that policies account for the diverse and overlapping challenges they face. By doing so, the initiative aims to create more equitable and inclusive solutions ; ones that reflect the complexities of poverty and social exclusion. Scope: This call for proposals aims at selecting and financially supporting a consortium consisting of organisations with proven and relevant competence and experience, including at European and/or international level, in facilitating the engagement of people with lived experience of poverty in policy discussions on challenges related to combating poverty and social inclusion. The consortium should consist of applicants capable of developing active participatory approach for people who have lived experience of poverty and actively contributing to their involvement in the Commission’s structured dialogue.
